latest.title: Controlling Differently: Internal Control Digitalization as a Dynamic Capability. A Conceptual Framework and Research Propositions
latest.venue: Revue Internationale des Sciences de Gestion
latest.abstract: The digitalization of internal control is widely presented as a lever of performance, yet the mechanisms behind this contribution remain unclear. This article argues that the dominant readings of the phenomenon, whether technical, compliance-based, or resource-based, share a common assumption: they treat digitalization as a state rather than as an ability, which prevents them from explaining why comparable tools produce different outcomes and why well-performing control systems become obsolete. Drawing on an integrative literature review and a theory adaptation approach, the article reinterprets internal control digitalization through dynamic capabilities theory. It distinguishes technological resources, operational capabilities, and dynamic capabilities, and defines internal control digitalization as a capability combining continuous risk sensing, deliberate response, and ongoing reconfiguration of the control system. This reinterpretation uncovers a tension between reconfiguration and the stability on which control reliability rests, and introduces the concept of reconfiguration governance, which is distinguished from IT change management and structured around five dimensions. Six propositions follow. The capability affects organizational performance mainly through two parallel and partial mediators, risk management effectiveness and internal control reliability, provided that data are of adequate quality and that automated controls remain under human oversight. Reconfiguration governance determines whether the capability strengthens or weakens control reliability, environmental dynamism moderates the relationship in an inverted U-shaped manner, and institutional pressures weaken it only when they lead to symbolic adoption. The article confronts these propositions wit

latest.title: Transformation of Business Communication Model in Crisis: Rebranding of Warung New Bahari into Ekspresss Bahari
latest.venue: Journal of Asian Multicultural Research for Economy and Management Study
latest.abstract: This study examines the transformation of the business communication model in the franchise crisis experienced by Warung New Bahari (WNB), which underwent rebranding into Ekspresss Bahari (WEB) and succeeded in maintaining only 30 of 125 outlets in the Jabodetabek region. Using a qualitative approach with a case study design, data were collected through in-depth interviews with 12 informants, participatory observation of 8 outlets, business document analysis, and two focus group discussions. Findings reveal that there is a structural disjunction between the implementation of Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) technology and the Cultural Intelligence (CQ) of organizational actors, manifested in seven forms of communication gaps. The transformation of the communication model was designed through three phases—restart-up, reconcept, and rebranding—by integrating CQ into every layer of business communication. The recommended communication model integrates ERP as a strategic communication platform, CQ as the core competence of organizational actors, and Artificial Intelligence (AI) as an operational enabler. The novelty of this research lies in bridging the studies of ERP, business communication, and cultural intelligence in the context of crisis, downsizing, and rebranding of franchise-based MSMEs.

latest.title: Bank complaint resolution outcomes and customer behavioural biases for accountable financial institutions in guwahati India
latest.venue: International Journal of Marketing Research Innovation
latest.abstract: Customer complaints against banks in India have risen sharply with the spread of digital banking, and accountable and transparent grievance redressal has become central to consumer protection and strong institutions. Earlier studies linked complaint handling to satisfaction and loyalty but paid little attention to how the outcome of a resolved complaint shapes the customer's later judgement. This study examines the influence of bank complaint resolution outcomes on four post-resolution behavioural biases: confirmation bias, loss aversion, overconfidence and complaint avoidance. Primary data were collected through a cross-sectional survey using a structured questionnaire from 547 customers across 329 branches of 12 public- and 12 private-sector banks in Guwahati City, India, who had lodged a formal complaint and were analysed using descriptive statistics, Cronbach's alpha and simple linear regression. The results show that 56.3% of complaints were fully resolved, 40.0% partially resolved, and 3.7% not resolved, and that the bias scales were reliable (α = 0.781 to 0.893). Complaint resolution outcome was positively related to confirmation bias (β = 0.764, R² = 0.584), loss aversion (β = 0.808, R² = 0.652) and overconfidence (β = 0.663, R² = 0.440), and negatively related to complaint avoidance (β = −0.783, R² = 0.613), all at p < 0.001. Loss aversion recorded the highest mean score (3.88) and confirmation bias the lowest (2.68). The findings suggest that complaint resolution outcomes account for 44.0% to 65.2% of the variation in post-resolution behavioural biases, indicating that resolving a complaint is a behavioural event, not just a procedural closure, within inclusive financial services. latest.title: Digital Transformation of Business Processes as a Factor in Increasing Competitiveness
latest.abstract: Purpose: This study examined the impact of business process digital transformation on the competitiveness of medium and large enterprises in Ukraine during 2021–2024. Design/Methodology/Approach: A quantitative panel econometric approach was applied using secondary financial and non-financial data for a balanced annual panel of 173 enterprises (692 observations). Integrated indices of digital transformation (five min–max normalised process indicators) and competitiveness (five z-standardised performance indicators) were constructed, and descriptive statistics, the Kolmogorov–Smirnov normality test, the Mann–Whitney U test for median-split groups, and, following the Hausman test, a fixed-effects regression with cluster-robust standard errors were employed. Research Limitations: The study was limited to medium and large Ukrainian enterprises and secondary data from 2021–2024. The estimates are associative rather than causal. Findings: Digitalisation increased steadily, competitiveness differed significantly across digitalisation levels, and the fixed-effects model showed a positive within-enterprise relationship between digital transformation and competitiveness. Higher digitalisation was associated with greater labour productivity, operating margins, revenue growth, and stronger market positions. Practical Implication: The findings support systematic digital modernisation as a strategy for improving enterprise competitiveness and can guide corporate digital strategies and policymaking. Social Implication: Business digitalisation may support organisational resilience, productivity, and sustainable economic development. Originality/Value: The study introduces the depth of digital integration of business processes as a variable, measured from enterprise reporting rather tha

latest.title: Customer relationship marketing and customer loyalty for inclusive and sustainable banking growth in Nigeria
latest.venue: International Journal of Marketing Research Innovation
latest.abstract: Competition, digital banking and rising customer expectations have made customer retention a central concern for Nigerian commercial banks, yet heavy spending on relationship programmes has not reduced complaints about service consistency and complaint handling, weakening the trust on which financial inclusion and sustainable growth depend. This study examines how customer relationship marketing dimensions, namely trust, commitment, communication, personalized services and customer engagement, influence customer satisfaction and customer loyalty and whether satisfaction mediates the link between relationship marketing and loyalty. A mixed-methods design was applied at the Jos branch of Access Bank Plc. Survey data from 277 customers were analysed with descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation and multiple regression, and interviews with 28 employees were analysed thematically. The results show that the five dimensions jointly explain 78.4% of the variance in customer satisfaction (F = 196.54, p < 0.001) and 81.1% of the variance in customer loyalty (F = 229.38, p < 0.001). Customer engagement is the strongest predictor of satisfaction (β = 0.392) and of loyalty (β = 0.341), followed by trust for satisfaction (β = 0.321) and personalized services for loyalty (β = 0.309). Satisfaction correlates strongly with loyalty (r = 0.918, p < 0.01), and the effect of relationship marketing on loyalty falls from 0.800 to 0.122 once satisfaction is controlled. Customers rated communication (mean = 4.00) and financial information security (mean = 3.88) higher than service consistency (mean = 3.72) and complaint handling (mean = 3.54). The findings suggest that relationship marketing builds loyalty mainly through satisfaction, with engagement, trust and personalized services carrying

latest.title: INDICADORES ANTECEDENTES NO APOIO À DECISÃO: PROJETO E AVALIAÇÃO DE UM ARTEFATO BASEADO EM REGRAS EM CAMPANHAS B2B COM CONVERSÃO OFFLINE
latest.abstract: Sistemas de apoio à decisão pressupõem que o resultado a ser otimizado esteja registrado pelo sistema operacional e disponível no momento da decisão. Este artigo investiga o projeto de um artefato decisório quando o desfecho ocorre fora do sistema, é raro e só se torna observável após o período de decisão. Adotou-se como método a Design Science Research. O artefato é uma árvore de decisão baseada em regras explícitas que combina retorno sobre investimento publicitário, volume e qualidade de leads, classificando cada período em escalar, otimizar, testar ou pausar. Foi instanciado sobre quinze meses de uma conta real de anúncios e avaliado por aplicação retroativa. A versão inicial convergiu com as decisões históricas em 27% dos períodos, pois o retorno mensal não discrimina desempenho quando o desfecho é raro. A versão revisada, com retorno acumulado, estado de resultado não observado e prioridade à qualidade, alcançou 47%, abaixo da regra trivial de sempre otimizar, indicando que a convergência mede aderência à prática, e não eficácia. Avaliadas pelo desfecho, as divergências favoreceram o artefato em um período e o desfavoreceram em outro. Conclui-se que a decisão nessas condições depende de indicadores antecedentes, cabendo ao indicador de resultado a função de confirmação posterior.

latest.title: SOCIAL SUSTAINABILITY REPORTING: A COMPARATIVE ANALYSIS OF THE GRI AND ESRS FRAMEWORKS
latest.venue: Facta Universitatis Series Economics and Organization
latest.abstract: Dynamic changes in the business environment and the steadily increasing pressure on companies to consider the social impacts of their business activities have intensified significantly in recent decades. Consequently, the importance of and need for non-financial information in this area have grown substantially. To ensure the comparability and consistency of sustainability reporting, appropriate reporting standards have been developed. Among these, the Global Reporting Initiative (GRI) Standards, which are voluntary in nature, have become the most widely adopted standards for sustainability reporting, including the reporting of the social dimension of sustainability. However, the recent introduction of the European Sustainability Reporting Standards (ESRS) may pose certain challenges for companies in the transition from voluntary to mandatory reporting standards. Accordingly, this paper aims to examine the main characteristics and significance of the GRI and ESRS frameworks and to highlight the similarities and differences between them in the area of social sustainability disclosures.

latest.title: Beyond the Click: How Brand Familiarity Bridges and Amplifies the Relationship Between Online Customer Experience and Shopping Behavior Across Three Asian Markets
latest.abstract: This study examines the influence of online customer experience on online shopping behavior and investigates the dual role of brand familiarity as both a mediating mechanism and a moderating condition across Pakistan, China, and Bangladesh.Data came from a cross-sectional survey of 887 online consumers from Pakistan (n = 308), China (n = 292), and Bangladesh (n = 287). Grounded in the Stimulus–Organism–Response (S-O-R) framework, the analysis used SPSS 28 and Hayes’ PROCESS macro: regression, bootstrapped mediation (Model 4), moderation (Model 1), and one-way ANOVA with Tukey post hoc tests.Online customer experience was positively associated with online shopping behavior (β = 0.60, p < 0.001) and brand familiarity (β = 0.57, p < 0.001). Brand familiarity was positively associated with online shopping behavior (β = 0.41, p < 0.001), partially mediating the relationship between online customer experience and online shopping behavior (indirect effect β = 0.23, 95% CI [0.15, 0.32]). Brand familiarity also strengthened this relationship (interaction β = 0.12, p < 0.001). Cross-country comparisons revealed significantly higher levels of all three constructs in China than in Pakistan and Bangladesh.This study extends the Stimulus–Organism–Response (S-O-R) framework by examining brand familiarity as an organismic state with two roles. It investigates whether brand familiarity mediates the relationship between online customer experience and shopping behavior and whether it strengthens that relationship. By examining these mechanisms in three Asian e-commerce markets at different stages of digital maturity, the study provides insight into how online experiences relate to shopping behavior. The findings also point to the value of combining high-quality online experiences with str

latest.title: AI-Driven Sensory Marketing and Consumer Purchase Intention in Lahore, Pakistan A PLS-SEM Approach
latest.abstract: This empirical study examines the influence of Artificial Intelligence (AI)–driven sensory marketing touchpoints on consumer purchase intentions among modern retail and fashion shoppers in Lahore, Pakistan. Grounded in the Stimulus-Organism-Response (S-O-R) framework and Aradhna Krishna’s sensory marketing theory, the study operationalizes AI-driven visual stimuli (AVS), AI-driven auditory stimuli (AAS), and AI virtual touch / augmented reality (AR) as exogenous stimuli that affect consumer emotional engagement (EE) as an organismic mediator, which in turn drives purchase intention (PI) as the behavioral response, moderated by consumer technology readiness (CTR). Primary quantitative data were collected via a structured survey from a sample of urban shoppers (N = 300) across major commercial hubs in Lahore, including Packages Mall, Emporium Mall, Y-Block DHA, and prominent online retail platforms. Data were evaluated using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) in SmartPLS 4. The empirical results demonstrate that the model explains 66.2% of the total variance in emotional engagement (R² = 0.662) and 56.1% of the variance in purchase intention (R² = 0.561). Both AI auditory stimuli (β = 0.597, p < 0.001) and AI visual stimuli (β = 0.342, p < 0.001) exert strong positive and statistically significant impacts on emotional engagement. Conversely, AI virtual touch / AR exhibits a marginally non-significant relationship (β = -0.116, p = 0.069), pointing to usability friction and digital adoption barriers in the local retail context. Emotional engagement strongly drives consumer purchase intentions (β = 0.587, p < 0.001), while Consumer Technology Readiness negatively moderates this relationship (β = -0.213, p < 0.001). latest.title: Profit-based ensemble and EMPC threshold optimization for hotel booking cancellation prediction
latest.abstract: This study proposes a profit-based ensemble model with integrated threshold optimization for hotel booking cancellation prediction. The proposed framework proposes a deployable intervention rule by directly maximizing the expected maximum profit criterion (EMPC) under a realistic payoff structure. Two base learners are trained using a cross-validation protocol to generate probability estimates. These risk estimates along with a single contextual engagement signal are integrated within the decision layer to produce an intervention score. A two-stage evolutionary learning strategy employing differential evolution is developed. The first stage optimizes a smooth surrogate of the EMPC to learn profit-aware ensemble weights, while the second stage selects the operating threshold by maximizing the EMPC. The model achieved EMPC of € 26.60 and area under the curve of 0.9288. Furthermore, our framework ensures explainability through feature importance analysis and interpretation of the decision-layer weights. The proposed framework offers a decision support system for hotel cancellation management.

latest.title: Employer branding and decent work across industries comparing ITC Limited and ICICI Bank in India
latest.venue: International Journal of Marketing Research Innovation
latest.abstract: Competition for skilled talent has made employer branding a strategic lever for decent work, gender equality and sustainable organisational reputation, yet comparative evidence on how industry context shapes the employer value proposition remains scarce in India. The study examines how the employer branding practices communicated by ITC Limited, a fast-moving consumer goods conglomerate, and ICICI Bank, a private-sector bank, converge and differ. A qualitative multiple-case design was applied to secondary data centred on the 2024–25 reporting year and drawn from ten categories of public documents, including annual reports, Business Responsibility and Sustainability Reports, career portals and official LinkedIn content. Passages were coded against fourteen literature-derived themes, eight internal and six external, and compared across nine cross-case themes. The results show that all nine themes (100%) appear in both organisations; two (22%), diversity and inclusion and employee well-being, converge in content, while seven (78%) diverge in emphasis. ICICI Bank reports about 42,000 women employees (32% of its workforce), more than 10 million learning hours and around 10 learning days per employee, a digital academy covering five technology domains and a recruitment platform with three support channels. ITC Limited anchors its proposition in leadership development through the KITES internship programme and ranked among the top three finalists for best employer brand on LinkedIn among organisations with more than 10,000 employees. The findings suggest that employer branding themes are shared across industries, whereas the content of the employer value proposition and the digital channels that carry it are shaped by industry-specific talent requirements. latest.title: Decoding anthropomorphism: a multidimensional perspective on presence, parasocial relationship and purchase intention
latest.abstract: Abstract Virtual influencers have become an increasingly important marketing tool, yet existing research has offered limited insight into how their anthropomorphic attributes should be conceptualized and through which psychological mechanisms they influence consumer responses. Addressing this gap, this study conceptualizes virtual influencer anthropomorphism as a multidimensional construct consisting of physical anthropomorphism, interactivity intelligence, and mental human-likeness, and examines its effects on purchase intention through social presence, telepresence, and parasocial relationship. Using online survey data, the results show that all three anthropomorphic attributes positively enhance consumers’ social presence and telepresence, which in turn strengthen parasocial relationships and subsequently increase purchase intention. The findings further refine the conceptualization of virtual influencer anthropomorphism by highlighting the importance of interaction-based anthropomorphism alongside visual and mental human-like cues. Overall, this study contributes to the literature by clarifying both the multidimensional nature of virtual influencer anthropomorphism and the psychological process through which it shapes consumer behavior.

latest.title: The psychology of AI-driven virtual endorsement: How narrative transportation shapes consumer engagement, brand perceptions, and purchase intentions among Gen-Z in Pakistan
latest.abstract: Purpose: Artificial intelligence (AI)-created virtual influencers are revolutionizing influencer marketing, but little is known about how their attributes relate to positive consumer reactions. Current studies have focused primarily on measures of engagement and credibility of the narrator and ignored the effect of immersive storytelling on the perceived endorsed brand. This study examines the effect of anthropomorphism, perceived authenticity and perceived similarity on the brand credibility, consumer engagement and purchase intention among Generation Z consumers in an emerging market, based on Narrative Transportation Theory. Design/methodology/approach: A quantitative, cross sectional study was conducted with 400 samples of Generation Z university students in Pakistan. Partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) was used to analyze data to explore the direct and indirect relationships. Results: The findings show that narrative transportation is the most important psychological mechanism that influences the consumer response to the characteristics of the virtual influencers. Both perceived authenticity and perceived similarity contribute to consumers' immersion in the virtual influencer's stories, which positively affects brand credibility, and thereby boosts consumer engagement and purchase intention. However, the unexpected negative effect of anthropomorphism on narrative transportation indicates that if too human-like, anthropomorphism can be detrimental to persuasive processing when using AI in influencer marketing. Originality/value: The study contributes to the existing knowledge on influencer marketing by applying the Narrative Transportation Theory to the virtual influencer context and by it assessing the role of immersive narrative experience

latest.title: PERSONALIZATION, PRIVACY AND TRUST IN AI-ASSISTED ONLINE SHOPPING: A CONCEPTUAL FRAMEWORK DISTINGUISHING TRUST IN THE ASSISTANT FROM TRUST IN THE RETAILER IN THE INDIAN CONTEXT
latest.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
authors: Soumya Sanoj and Dr S. Alakendran
latest.abstract: Abstract AI-enabled shopping assistants now help consumers discover products, compare options and ask questions during online purchases. Whether shoppers act on that help depends on how relevant and how personal the advice feels, how well the assistant performs, and what shoppers believe is happening to their data. This conceptual paper develops a stimulus–organism–response framework for AI-assisted online shopping in India. It links two dimensions of perceived personalization (relevance and specificity) and chatbot quality to privacy concerns and trust, and through them to purchase intention. The paper makes three contributions. First, it separates trust in the assistant from trust in the retailer that deploys it. Second, it treats chatbot quality as a construct distinct from personalization and grounds it in research on AI chatbot service quality. Third, it brings together two roles of trust that earlier studies have specified separately, trust as a mediator and trust as a buffer against privacy concerns, in one model with a stated causal order and a route to testing. The framework draws on the technology acceptance model, trust research, privacy-calculus and privacy-boundary reasoning, and the computers-are-social-actors paradigm, and it is positioned against recent peer-reviewed studies of chatbots and shopping assistants, including studies of Indian shoppers. Eight propositions, boundary conditions, measurement guidance and an analytic strategy are offered for empirical work. India, where the Digital Personal Data Protection Rules, 2025 are phasing in notice-and-consent duties, is a timely setting in which to test them. Keywords: AI shopping assistants; perceived personalization; chatbot quality; privacy concerns; consumer trust; purchase intention; personalization

latest.title: CONTENT MARKETING DIMENSIONS AND CUSTOMER PATRONAGE OF QUICK-SERVICE RESTAURANTS IN CALABAR, NIGERIA
latest.venue: Journal of Management Science and Entrepreneurship
latest.abstract: This study examined the effect of content marketing on customer patronage of quick-service restaurants (QSRs) in Calabar, Cross River State, Nigeria. Specifically, it assessed the effects of informational content marketing, visual content marketing and social media content marketing on customer patronage. A cross-sectional survey design was adopted, and primary data were collected from customers of purposively selected QSR outlets using a structured questionnaire. The sample size was determined using the Topman formula, resulting in 369 questionnaires being administered, of which 328 were returned and found usable, representing a response rate of 88.9%. The data were analysed using descriptive statistics and multiple linear regression with the Statistical Package for the Social Sciences (SPSS). The regression model was statistically significant (F = 35.640, p < .001), explaining 24.8% of the variation in customer patronage (R² = .248). The findings revealed that informational content marketing (Beta = .163, p = .010), visual content marketing (Beta = .288, p = .001) and social media content marketing (Beta = .372, p = .002) each had a positive and statistically significant effect on customer patronage. Social media content marketing recorded the strongest relative contribution, followed by visual and informational content marketing. The study concludes that content marketing is an important factor associated with customer patronage of QSRs in Calabar, with social media content marketing demonstrating the greatest relative contribution among the dimensions examined. It recommends that QSR operators enhance their informational content, strengthen the visual appeal of their marketing materials and reinforce their social media content strategies to encourage customer prefer

latest.title: Improving the Automatic Classification of Interviewer Questions in Avatar‐Based Child Investigative Interview Simulations: A Transformer Approach
latest.abstract: Abstract Purpose Interviewer questioning style, including the types of questions asked, represents one measurable and trainable component of child investigative interview quality. Although automated approaches to question classification have been explored, previous systems have shown only moderate performance, particularly when distinguishing fine‐grained categories of questions. The present study aimed to improve the automatic multi‐class classification of interviewer questions and the detection of repetitive questioning patterns in avatar‐based simulations of child sexual abuse investigative interviews using transformer‐based architectures. Method The system was trained on 17,425 annotated questions derived from controlled avatar‐based interview simulations and categorized into 14 question‐category labels. A transformer model (F2LLM‐0.6B) was fine‐tuned for multi‐class classification using weighted loss to address class imbalance. A separate LLM‐based module (Qwen3.5‐9B) detected semantically repeated or reformulated questions within interview sequences. Performance was evaluated using accuracy, macro‐ and weighted F1‐scores, and confusion matrix analyses. On a held‐out test set ( N = 2, 614), the classification model achieved an overall accuracy of 86.8% and a macro‐F1 score of 79.0%, while the repetition‐detection module achieved an accuracy of 84.9%. Conclusions These findings indicate that AI systems can approximate the available human‐coded reference labels for interviewer question types and identify repeated or reformulated questioning patterns. The system supports taxonomy‐based coding of interviewer questions; it does not independently determine their pragmatic or contextual appropriateness within the broader interview sequence, nor does it assess overall inte

latest.title: When do e-commerce prediction models fail over time? cross-task evidence on temporal reliability and model maintenance
latest.abstract: Machine-learning models in e-commerce are often evaluated on randomly partitioned historical data, whereas deployment requires prediction on future observations under changing populations and information availability. We examine temporal reliability and model maintenance across four public dataset–task settings: late-delivery prediction among eventually delivered Olist orders, matched 24-h cart-to-purchase prediction in Retailrocket and Synerise RecSys 2025, and 30-day repeat-purchase prediction in Online Retail II. Sequential analyses restrict historical features, model updating, and recalibration to information and labels available at each prediction or deployment time. Random-to-future differences varied substantially: Olist showed pronounced deterioration, whereas the other settings showed smaller or qualitatively different changes. In the primary Olist XGBoost analysis, cumulative retraining improved ranking and modestly improved Brier accuracy, while sliding-window retraining improved ranking but worsened probability reliability. Cross-model, matched-exposure, and sensitivity analyses showed that maintenance effects depended on setting, period, model family, and design. Post-hoc recalibration did not provide a consistently reliable repair, and same-base calibration effects differed from net maintenance-policy effects. The matched comparisons do not identify causal task or duration effects. These findings support forward-in-time evaluation that assesses ranking, probability quality, label availability, and maintenance effects separately rather than inferring future reliability from offline performance or task identity.

latest.title: FRUGAL INNOVATIONS AS A PATHWAY TO INCLUSIVE AND RESOURCE-EFFICIENT ENTREPRENEURSHIP
latest.venue: Facta Universitatis Series Economics and Organization
latest.abstract: This paper examines frugal innovation as a pathway to inclusive and resource-efficient entrepreneurship in widening economies. Building on a structured literature review, the study conceptualises frugal innovation within sustainability and innovation ecosystem perspectives and empirically tests key relationships using survey data from universities/technology transfer offices and start-ups.The results show that only selected mechanisms are statistically supported. Educational and mentoring support is positively associated with frugal innovation capability development, while business model development significantly contributes to innovation outputs. In contrast, expected relationships related to frugal design, user involvement, and measurement practices are not confirmed.These findings reveal a systemic implementation gap: although frugal innovation principles are widely recognised, they are not yet effectively integrated into coherent innovation processes. The weak role of metrics further indicates underdeveloped evaluation frameworks.The study contributes by identifying structural misalignments in frugal innovation ecosystems and provides policy-relevant insights for strengthening their practical implementation in widening contexts.

latest.title: INSURANCE COMPANY AS A SOFTWARE SOLUTION
latest.venue: Facta Universitatis Series Economics and Organization
latest.abstract: Digital transformation within the insurance industry often follows predictable pathways that mirror established business model blueprints. Most innovation efforts target specific segments of the insurance value chain. Consequently, few full-stack insurance companies are built entirely on Insurtech principles, and virtually no organisations operate beyond this level. This paper investigates the future of insurance by introducing the concept model of Insurance Company as a Software Solution (ICaSS). By extrapolating current achievements in insurance automation, this study explores the future trajectory of the industry and outlines key conclusions.

latest.title: AI and Stress
latest.abstract: ABSTRACT Given the spread of artificial intelligence (AI) tools at work, understanding their health implications is critically important. We use rich survey data from Finland and apply propensity score matching that accounts for observable differences between regular AI users and non‐users to estimate the relationship between reported AI usage at work and workers’ reported stress. Regular AI use is associated with a 4.4 percentage point higher probability of reporting stress, equivalent to a 25.6% increase relative to baseline. Comparing two competing explanations, we find that this pattern is more consistent with heavier work demands than with concerns about job loss: AI use is associated with more unpaid work outside working hours and, less precisely, with intense work absorption, but not with job insecurity. Exploratory subgroup estimates are larger and individually significant for men, non‐supervisors, unionized workers and employees in medium‐sized workplaces, although the differences across subgroups are not statistically significant.

latest.title: Green Entrepreneurship as a Catalyst for Local Environmental Management in South Africa: Opportunities, Barriers, and Policy Implications
latest.abstract: ABSTRACT Building on the question of how environmental management can be addressed at the local level, the transition from a linear “take–make–dispose” model to a circular economy ( CE ) has become central to sustainable development, particularly in emerging economies facing intertwined environmental and socioeconomic challenges. In South Africa, high unemployment, energy security, and escalating waste generation intensify the urgency for systemic restructuring. This study examines green entrepreneurship (GE) as a catalyst for CE development within environmental management, focusing on Limpopo Province as a contextually rich case of resource potential and developmental vulnerability. Using a qualitative design grounded in thematic analysis, data were collected from 40 green entrepreneurs and 10 policymakers across recycling, renewable energy, sustainable agriculture, green manufacturing, and governance sectors. Findings reveal a layered circular ecosystem comprising downstream resource recovery (recycling and waste management), midstream production transformation (renewable energy and regenerative agriculture), and upstream systemic enablers (consultancy and ecodesign services). These activities represent distinct circular business model innovations through which firms create environmental value by recovering resources, extending product life cycles, substituting fossil‐based inputs, and redesigning production processes. Findings indicate that green entrepreneurs implement a range of CE practices, including resource recovery, renewable‐energy provision, composting, and environmentally oriented manufacturing. Participants reported that these activities contributed to waste reduction, resource efficiency, and environmental sustainability. However, these reported outcomes

latest.title: Extending reach while maintaining oversight: Clinicians' perspectives on digital mental health implementation in youth services
latest.abstract: Background Digital mental health interventions (DMHIs) offer a promising means of extending care for children and adolescents, yet their integration into routine clinical services remains inconsistent. The implementation conditions clinicians identify as prerequisites for adoption carry greater relevance given the emergence of AI tools now being used by young people. This study examined the perspectives of mental health professionals (MHPs) working with children and young people to identify key implementation considerations for the development and adoption of DMHIs. Methods Nineteen focus groups were conducted with 50 mental health clinicians from a range of service settings in Queensland, Australia between May 2020 and May 2021. Data were analyzed using a mixed deductive-inductive thematic approach informed by the Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research (CFIR). Results MHPs were cautiously optimistic about DMHIs, viewing them as most valuable when implemented as supplementary rather than replacement tools. Key perceived uses included waitlist support, screening and assessment, between-session engagement, and flexible treatment pathways. However, MHPs consistently emphasized the need to preserve clinical judgement and oversight across all stages of DMHI use. Risk management, duty of care, and privacy and confidentiality were identified as critical prerequisites for implementation. Conclusions Successful DMHI implementation in child and adolescent mental health services requires flexible, clinician-centered integration approaches, robust risk management protocols, and clear organizational frameworks delineating clinician responsibility. keywords: child and adolescent mental health services

latest.title: Analysis of HR Administration Implementation in Workload Management and Work Communication in the Rooms Department Division of Anara Sky Kualanamu Hotel
latest.venue: International Journal of Management Research and Economics
latest.abstract: This study aims to analyze the implementation of Human Resources (HR) administration regarding workload management and workplace communication within the Rooms Division of Anara Sky Kualanamu Hotel. The study is contextualized by the dynamic operational nature of the hotel industry-specifically within the Rooms Division, which faces fluctuating workloads due to changes in occupancy rates, guest service requirements, and work schedules. Furthermore, effective workplace communication is crucial for supporting staff coordination and operational smoothness. Poorly managed workloads and ineffective communication can lead to misunderstandings, hinder coordination, and potentially impact service quality. This study employs a qualitative method with a descriptive approach. Informants were selected using purposive sampling, involving individuals with direct knowledge and experience regarding HR administration, workload management, and workplace communication within the Rooms Division. Data collection was conducted through interviews, observation, and documentation. A qualitative approach was utilized to gain an in-depth understanding of HR administration practices, as well as the informants' experiences and perceptions regarding actual working conditions.
latest.subfield: Organizational Behavior and Human Resource Management

latest.title: Public discourse on violence in medical settings and its implications for medical students' career resilience: evidence from social media text mining
latest.abstract: Background Violence in medical settings has become a growing concern, yet the potential relevance of this public discourse to the career-development environment surrounding medical students remains underexplored. This study investigates the external discursive environment surrounding medical violence and its potential implications for medical students' professional identity and resilience. Methods This study used computational text analysis of public comments on Sina Weibo about violence in medical settings. Guided LDA was applied to 13,101 comments containing at least one retained vocabulary term, while sentiment analysis was conducted on 14,115 comments with usable token sequences. Career Adaptability and Psychological Capital theories informed seed-word selection and the interpretation of the findings. Results Three primary topics emerged: occupational safety (32.9%), professional ethics (30.3%), and professional identification (36.8%) under dominant-topic assignment. Positive sentiment accounted for 63.9% of comments, negative sentiment for 33.1%, and neutral sentiment for 3.0%. Conclusions Positive sentiment predominated, but substantial negative sentiment remained. These patterns characterize a heterogeneous external discursive environment potentially relevant to medical students' career resilience, without establishing individual effects.

latest.title: Strategic Agility and Sustainable Performance of Manufacturing Firms in Nakuru County, Kenya
latest.venue: International Journal of Social Science and Humanities Research (IJSSHR)
latest.abstract: Strategic agility is the capacity of a firm to sense changes in its operating environment, anticipate alternative futures and reconfigure its resources and operations in good time. It has become a critical capability for manufacturing firms, which operate in an increasingly uncertain environment characterised by economic instability, supply chain disruptions, climate variability and rising production costs. In Nakuru County, Kenya, many manufacturing firms still respond to such disruptions reactively, and evidence on how agility practices relate to their ability to sustain performance remains limited. Therefore, the purpose of this study was to examine the influence of strategic agility on sustainable performance of manufacturing firms in Nakuru County, Kenya. It explored four practices, namely environmental scanning, scenario planning, strategic flexibility and early warning systems. The study was anchored on Dynamic Capabilities Theory, Complexity Theory, the Resource-Based View and Organizational Learning Theory. The study adopted a descriptive and explanatory research design and targeted the 34 manufacturing firms in the county. A census of the firms was undertaken and four managers, comprising senior, operations and strategy managers, were purposively selected from each firm, giving 136 respondents, of whom 96 returned completed questionnaires. Structured questionnaires were used to collect data. Both descriptive and inferential statistical methods were used to analyse the data, which were presented in tables and discussed. The findings revealed that the four practices jointly explained 43.9% of the variation in sustainable performance. Environmental scanning was the strongest predictor of sustainable performance, followed by scenario planning and early warning sys

latest.title: Seeking Social Sustainability in the Palm Oil Supply Chain: An Assessment of Whistleblowing Intentions in an Indonesian Setting
authors: Ana Beatriz Lopes de Sousa Jabbour
latest.abstract: ABSTRACT Whistleblowing has long been an effective method of exposing wrongdoing and unethical practices in organizations. However, it has not been widely studied as a mechanism for identifying social issues in supply chains, such as modern slavery taking place in controversial sectors, including the palm oil industry in Indonesia, the key region for the global palm oil industry. Therefore, a large‐scale survey with employees working in the palm oil plantation sector was conducted to assess employees' reactions and behavioral responses to a modern slavery scenario. A hypothetical scenario was created, asking employees to position themselves as a witness to a situation related to human exploitation and forced labor in their workplace. The findings confirm a direct positive relationship between the perceived seriousness of wrongdoing (PSW) and the intention to leave and report, where PSW related to modern slavery prompted observers to opt out before speaking up. This paper advances the debate on tackling modern slavery by addressing this issue from both a whistleblowing and an employees' sensemaking perspective.
latest.subfield: Organizational Behavior and Human Resource Management

latest.title: FinTech Development and Corporate Innovation: Implications for ESG Performance and Financial Resilience - An Exploratory Study of Indian Listed Companies
latest.abstract: The study being reviewed has both theoretical and practical qualities. The study aims to introduce the framework linking Fintech evolution to corporate innovation and ESG performance, along with the financial resilience testing through the analysis of empirical data from India. There are nine companies that do not have relations to financial activities of the study. All of them will be analysed in the period of FY2023-FY2025 (27 case studies). To analyse these 27 companies ROA and operating margin ratio will be used along with statistical procedures. The data for fiscal years FY2023-FY2025 reveals that the sales growth was 15.39%, operating profit growth was at the level of 16.97%, the net profit growth constituted 33.76%, and cash flows growth equalled 37.91%, while borrowing decreased by 9.90%. The Debt/Assets ratio fell from 15.49% to 12.55% (p = 0.049, Cohen’s dz = −0.77). The relationship between ROA and CFO/assets was very strong (r = 0.774, p < 0.001) and the inverse relationship between ROA and the ratio of Debt/assets (r = −0.631, p < 0.001) was confirmed using rank-based tests. The results indicate that it is possible to achieve financial resilience and present a clear empirical basis for general claims about links between FinTech, innovation, and ESG. The study must avoid unfounded causal claims and establish a basis for future research with larger samples in India.

latest.title: Accelerating Sustainability Transitions in Resource‐Constrained and Institutionally Fragile Markets: The Role of ESG Strategies and Sustainable Innovation
latest.abstract: ABSTRACT The increasing global emphasis on corporate sustainability has positioned environmental, social, and governance (ESG) performance as a critical element of corporate governance and long‐term value creation. However, firms in emerging economies, particularly those within sub‐Saharan Africa (SSA) under the Belt and Road Initiative (BRI), continue to face challenges in advancing ESG practices due to institutional weaknesses, governance complexities, and financing constraints. This study examines the impact of corporate ownership structure on ESG performance among 497 manufacturing firms in SSA BRI economies from 2013 to 2023. It further investigates the mediating role of innovation capacity, represented by technological innovation and environmental innovation, and the moderating role of financing decisions, measured by equity and debt financing. Grounded in the resource‐based view, stakeholder theory, and institutional theory, the study employs dynamic generalized method of moments (GMM) estimation to address endogeneity concerns and applies MMQR to capture heterogeneous effects. The findings reveal that management, state, family, and foreign ownership positively influence ESG performance, whereas institutional and blockholder ownership negatively affect ESG outcomes. Technological and environmental innovation significantly mediate the ownership–ESG relationship. Furthermore, equity financing strengthens this relationship, whereas debt financing weakens it. The study also identifies significant heterogeneity across regional, policy, and industry contexts. The study contributes to corporate sustainability literature by integrating ownership structures, innovation capacity, and financing decisions into the ESG framework. latest.title: Artificial Intelligence Adoption and Financial Decision-Making Quality among SMEs in Freetown, Sierra Leone: The Moderating Role of Digital Capability
latest.venue: Bulletin of Social Studies and Community Development
latest.abstract: This study investigates the impact of artificial intelligence (AI) adoption on financial decision-making quality (FDMQ) among small and medium enterprises (SMEs) in Freetown, Sierra Leone. It examines the moderating role of digital capability. The study used a quantitative, cross-sectional survey design with a sample of 250 owner-managers and finance officers from SMEs in formal and semi-formal business clusters in Freetown, based on the Technology–Organization–Environment (TOE) framework and Resource-Based View (RBV). The data were analyzed using SPSS with descriptive statistics, correlation analysis, and hierarchical moderated multiple regression. Findings showed that AI adoption (β = .573, p .001) and digital capability (β = .283, p .001) were significant, positive predictors of FDMQ. The AI adoption–FDMQ relationship was also significantly moderated by digital capability (β = .195, ΔR² = .035, p .001). Simple slopes analysis showed that the effect of AI adoption was more than doubled when digital capability increased from low to high. AI adoption enhances SME financial decision-making, but its impact relies on supporting digital capabilities. The study builds on the TOE and RBV frameworks in an under-researched West African context. It emphasizes the importance of integrating AI provision with digital capability development. Findings suggest associations, not causal or broadly generalizable effects, because of the cross-sectional, self-reported design and the Freetown sample. Keywords: artificial intelligence; financial decision-making; digital capability; smes, sierra leone.

latest.title: The effects of generative AI cues on consumer flow in E-commerce platforms: findings from experiments
DIGITAL TECHNOLOGY ADOPTION IN MICROENTERPRISES: A BIBLIOMETRIC AND THEMATIC REVIEW OF DIGITAL MARKETING AND FINTECH RESEARCH
latest.venue: International Journal of Small and Medium Enterprises
latest.abstract: Microenterprises are a fundamental component of economic development in emerging economies because they generate employment, foster innovation, and contribute to GDP. However, their limited resources make it difficult to keep pace with the rapidly expanding digital economy, and research on their adoption of digital marketing and financial technology (FinTech) remains fragmented. This study examines the evolution and thematic structure of the literature on digital marketing and FinTech adoption in microenterprises. Following the PRISMA guidelines, 499 records published between 2010 and 2026 were retrieved from the Scopus database using two search strings; after duplicate and ineligible records were removed, 337 documents were subjected to bibliometric analysis, and 159 full-text documents were reviewed thematically. The results show that the field grew at an annual rate of 26.87%, with an average document age of 2.16 years and 17.42 citations per document. The documents were written by 1,123 authors, and journal articles accounted for 68.84% (232 documents). The 985 author keywords formed three co-occurrence clusters centered on digital marketing, FinTech and financial inclusion, and FinTech adoption and financial literacy. The findings of this study suggest that the field is young, fast-growing, and highly collaborative and that it converges on four themes: digital marketing adoption and performance transformation; FinTech-driven financial inclusion and entrepreneurial development; financial literacy, FinTech adoption, and sustainable business development; and the strategic integration of digital technologies for marketing performance. hot.title: How generative AI Is shaping the future of marketing
hot.venue: Journal of the Academy of Marketing Science
hot.abstract: Abstract Generative AI (Gen AI) is shaping the future of marketing. In the next decade, Gen AI will influence how marketers interact and communicate with customers, help create and deliver marketing content (text, images, and video), and inform methods for researching and developing new products and services. In both service and sales settings, Gen AI will affect customers directly and significantly. Therefore, marketers, researchers, and public policy makers require a clear understanding of Gen AI and its potential, as well as its limitations. To assist marketers in thinking through the adoption and implementation of Gen AI, the current article presents a four-quadrant organizing framework that highlights trade-offs in both the nature of Gen AI inputs and the extent of human augmentation needed to deliver Gen AI–generated outputs. This framework provides guidance for the selection and implementation of Gen AI tools, as well as recommendations for further research.

hot.title: Interaction with AI companions and psychological well-being
AI Companions Reduce Loneliness
hot.abstract: Abstract Chatbots are now able to engage in sophisticated conversations with consumers in the domain of relationships, providing a potential coping solution to widescale societal loneliness. Behavioral research provides little insight into whether these applications (apps) are effective at alleviating loneliness. We address this question by focusing on “artificial intelligence (AI) companions”: apps designed to provide consumers with synthetic interaction partners. Study 1 examines user reviews of AI companion apps and finds correlational evidence suggesting that these apps help alleviate loneliness. Study 2 finds that AI companions successfully alleviate loneliness on par only with interacting with another person and more than other activities such as watching YouTube videos. Moreover, consumers underestimate the degree to which AI companions improve their loneliness. Study 3 uses a longitudinal design and finds that an AI companion consistently provides momentary reductions in loneliness after use over the course of a week. Study 4 provides evidence that both the chatbots’ performance and, especially, whether it makes users feel heard, explain reductions in loneliness. Study 5 provides an additional robustness check for the loneliness-alleviating benefits of AI companions and shows that self-disclosure and distraction alone do not explain AI companions’ effectiveness.

hot.title: Leading in the Digital Age: The Role of Leadership in Organizational Digital Transformation
hot.abstract: In the modern digital age, organizations face unprecedented challenges and possibilities while managing the intricacies of digital transformation. Accelerated technological developments, changing customer preferences, heightened competition, and dynamic regulatory environments necessitate companies to synchronize their business goals with technological innovations. Leadership is crucial in steering businesses through changes, requiring a deep understanding of change processes and the capacity to adjust leadership accordingly. This research addresses the central question: How does leadership effectively promote organizational digital transformation? The study examines how leaders can effectively promote the adoption of advanced technologies and the promotion of innovation, by first exploring the nature of digital transformation within organizations and then analyzing the evolving dynamics of leadership in this context. An integrative review of the Web of Science (WoS) and Scopus databases was conducted, using the search terms: “Leadership” and “Digital Transformation”. The findings emphasize that effective leadership is crucial for managing the minutiae of digital transformation, integrating technology into organizational processes to facilitate learning, collaboration, and agility, enabling companies to adapt to market shifts, reduce uncertainty, and enhance decision-making for sustainable growth. By using the right tools and with the right frequency, leaders may develop team cohesion—even at a distance. Attentive digital-age leaders will know how to leverage the right mechanisms, and herein, we hope to give some indication of how that may be achieved, so that digital transformation increases rather than decreases team motivation levels.

hot.title: Why human–AI relationships need socioaffective alignment
hot.abstract: Humans strive to design safe AI systems that align with our goals and remain under our control. However, as AI capabilities advance, we face a new challenge: the emergence of deeper, more persistent relationships between humans and AI systems. We explore how increasingly capable AI agents may generate the perception of deeper relationships with users, especially as AI becomes more personalised and agentic. This shift, from transactional interaction to ongoing sustained social engagement with AI, necessitates a new focus on socioaffective alignment—how an AI system behaves within the social and psychological ecosystem co-created with its user, where preferences and perceptions evolve through mutual influence. Addressing these dynamics involves resolving key intrapersonal dilemmas, including balancing immediate versus long-term well-being, protecting autonomy, and managing AI companionship alongside the desire to preserve human social bonds. By framing these challenges through a notion of basic psychological needs, we seek AI systems that support, rather than exploit, our fundamental nature as social and emotional beings.

hot.title: A Closer Look into Recent Video-based Learning Research: A Comprehensive Review of Video Characteristics, Tools, Technologies, and Learning Effectiveness
hot.venue: International Journal of Artificial Intelligence in Education
hot.abstract: People increasingly use videos on the Web for learning, be it for daily tasks in formal or informal educational settings. To enhance this type of learning, scientists are continuously conducting experiments, proposing guidelines, analyzing data, and researching artificial intelligence methods for tool development. In this comprehensive review, we analyze 257 articles (using PRISMA guidelines) on video-based learning from a technological perspective for the period from 2016 to 2021. One of the aims is to identify video characteristics that support learning as explored by previous research. Based on our analysis, we suggest a taxonomy that organizes the video characteristics and contextual aspects into eight categories: (1) audio features, (2) visual features, (3) textual features, (4) instructor behavior, (5) learners’ activities (play, pause, etc.), (6) interactive features (quizzes, etc.), (7) production style, and (8) instructional design. Also, we identify four representative methodological approaches: (1) tool support of video-based learning, (2) controlled experiments, (3) data analysis studies, and (4) design guidelines for learning videos. We find that the most explored characteristics are textual features followed by visual features, learners’ activities, and interactive features. Tools that aid learning through videos frequently utilize text from transcripts, video frames, and images. The learner’s activity is heavily explored through log files in data analysis studies, and interactive features are frequently scrutinized in controlled experiments. As further contributions, we contrast research findings on how video characteristics affect learning effectiveness, report on tasks and technologies used to develop tools, and summarize design guideline trends to prod

hot.title: The moderating role of personalized recommendations in the trust–satisfaction–loyalty relationship: an empirical study of AI-driven e-commerce
hot.abstract: Abstract Purpose This study investigates the effects of trust, satisfaction, and loyalty on AI-driven e-commerce, with a particular focus on how personalized recommendations moderate these relationships. It aims to explore how personalized AI features reshape consumer perceptions and decision-making. Design/methodology/approach A quantitative research approach was used to collect data from a diverse group of e-commerce users who had interacted with AI-based recommendation systems. An online survey employing standardized scales for trust, satisfaction, loyalty, and personalization was administered, and data were analyzed using structural equation modeling (SEM) to test the hypotheses. Findings The study reveals that trust has a significant positive influence on both satisfaction and loyalty. Personalization further strengthens these relationships by moderating the trust–satisfaction–loyalty dynamic. Satisfaction partially mediates the relationship between trust and loyalty, with the model’s explanatory power improving by 5% when personalization is included as a moderator. These results highlight the pivotal role of personalized recommendations in shaping consumer trust and satisfaction in AI-driven e-commerce. Practical implications Businesses can use personalized recommendation systems to enhance trust and satisfaction, thereby fostering loyalty. For example, platforms like Amazon and Netflix have successfully employed personalized AI algorithms to boost customer retention and engagement. Transparency features, such as explaining why certain products are recommended, and cultural sensitivity in algorithm design can further enhance customer trust and acceptance. e-commerce organizations should also invest in data privacy measures and clear algorithms to maintain consumer

hot.title: The Typing Cure: Experiences with Large Language Model Chatbots for Mental Health Support
hot.venue: Proceedings of the ACM on Human-Computer Interaction
hot.abstract: People experiencing severe distress increasingly use Large Language Model (LLM) chatbots as mental health support tools. Discussions on social media have described how engagements were lifesaving for some, but evidence suggests that general-purpose LLM chatbots also have notable risks that could endanger the welfare of users if not designed responsibly. In this study, we investigate the lived experiences of people who have used LLM chatbots for mental health support. We build on interviews with 21 individuals from globally diverse backgrounds to analyze how users create unique support roles for their chatbots, fill in gaps in everyday care, and navigate associated cultural limitations when seeking support from chatbots. We ground our analysis in psychotherapy literature around effective support, and introduce the concept of therapeutic alignment, or aligning AI with therapeutic values for mental health contexts. Our study offers recommendations for how designers can approach the ethical and effective use of LLM chatbots and other AI mental health support tools in mental health care.

hot.title: AI-driven personalization: Unraveling consumer perceptions in social media engagement
Confronting and alleviating AI resistance in the workplace: An integrative review and a process framework
hot.abstract: This study involves an integrative literature review and a process framework explaining the mechanisms to confront and alleviate employee Artificial intelligence (AI) resistance in organizations. First, we conceptualize AI resistance as a three-dimensional concept embodied in employees' fears, inefficacies, and antipathies toward AI. We advance that experiencing mistrust, existential questioning, and technological reflection are key individual mechanisms to confronting AI resistance connected to organizational mechanisms to alleviate AI resistance through the continuous interaction and unfolding of anxiety and introspection. We also explain the alleviation of AI resistance as an organizational process consisting of AI accessibility, human-AI augmentation, and AI-technology legitimation, each of which maps into one of the dimensions in the employee-level confrontation mechanisms. Overall, our conceptual framework provides an overarching and granular understanding of AI resistance, how employees confront it, and how it can be alleviated in the workplace. • Develops a process framework explaining the mechanisms to confront and alleviate employee AI resistance. • AI resistance as a three-dimensional concept embodied in employees' fears, inefficacies, and antipathies toward AI. • Highlights mistrust, existential questioning, and technological reflection as key individual concerns • AI resistance is alleviated through AI accessibility, human-AI augmentation, and AI-technology legitimation.
