latest.title: Model AISAS dalam Proses Pembentukan Loyalitas Pelanggan pada Akun @Warunghasturi
latest.abstract: Perkembangan media sosial mendorong pelaku usaha kuliner memanfaatkan komunikasi pemasaran digital untuk menarik perhatian konsumen dan mempertahankan loyalitas pelanggan. Penelitian ini bertujuan menganalisis komunikasi pemasaran digital melalui akun Instagram @warunghasturi berdasarkan model Attention, Interest, Search, Action, dan Share (AISAS) serta mengidentifikasi faktor-faktor pendukung pelaksanaannya dalam meningkatkan loyalitas pelanggan. Penelitian ini menggunakan pendekatan kualitatif dengan pengumpulan data melalui observasi, wawancara terstruktur, dan dokumentasi. Informan terdiri atas enam orang yang meliputi pemilik usaha, admin Instagram, pekerja, pengikut Instagram, dan konsumen. Data dianalisis menggunakan model interaktif Miles dan Huberman melalui reduksi data, penyajian data, serta penarikan kesimpulan. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa Warung Hasturi telah menerapkan kelima tahapan AISAS melalui konten visual, informasi produk, interaksi dengan pengikut, promosi, dan unggahan pengalaman pelanggan. Faktor pendukungnya meliputi konsistensi pengelolaan konten, kreativitas dan keragaman unggahan, interaksi dua arah, serta penyampaian informasi dan promosi produk. Loyalitas pelanggan terlihat dari pembelian ulang, kunjungan kembali, dan rekomendasi kepada orang lain. Penelitian ini menyimpulkan bahwa komunikasi pemasaran digital melalui Instagram dapat mendukung loyalitas pelanggan apabila diimbangi dengan kualitas produk, pelayanan, kenyamanan outlet, dan kesiapan operasional usaha.

latest.title: Pengaruh Green Brand Image dan Perceived Taste Quality dalam Membentuk Repurchase Intention Konsumen Fore Coffee
authors: I Dewa Ayu Shanti Kumala Prabaswari
Ni Putu Eka Ayu Chandra Wijaya
Ni Komang Trisa Bali Meyin Dandra Tirta
latest.abstract: Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menganalisis dampak citra merek ramah lingkungan (Green Brand Image) dan kualitas rasa produk (Perceived Taste Quality) terhadap loyalitas pelanggan Fore Coffee di Kota Denpasar. Penelitian ini bersifat kuantitatif, yang meneliti hubungan sebab-akibat antarvariabel melalui pengujian hipotesis. Dari populasi konsumen Fore Coffee di Kota Denpasar, sebanyak 112 individu dipilih sebagai responden dengan menggunakan teknik purposive sampling. Responden yang terpilih merupakan individu berusia 17 tahun yang saat ini pernah mengonsumsi produk minuman di Fore Coffee lebih dari satu kali. Instrumen penelitian dievaluasi menggunakan uji validitas, uji reliabilitas, dan uji asumsi klasik, sementara data dilakukan menggunakan regresi linear berganda, dengan hipotesis yang diuji menggunakan uji F dan uji t. Seluruh analisis statistik dilakukan menggunakan perangkat lunak SPSS. Hasil temuan ini menunjukkan bahwa kualitas rasa menjadi salah satu pertimbangan penting bagi konsumen dalam menentukan minat untuk kembali membeli produk Fore Coffee. Oleh karena itu, perusahaan perlu menjaga konsistensi rasa dan terus mengembangkan kualitas produk sekaligus mempertahankan komitmen terhadap praktik ramah lingkungan guna meningkatkan minat beli ulang konsumen

latest.title: The effect of independence, integrity, and competence on audit quality with auditor client retention as a moderating variable
latest.abstract: This study aims to examine and analyze the effect of auditor independence, integrity, and competence on audit quality, as well as the moderating role of audit client retention. The occurrence of various audit failure cases and inconsistent results in prior research provide the background for this study. A quantitative survey approach was employed. Data were collected via questionnaires administered to auditors working at Public Accounting Firms (KAPs) in the DKI Jakarta area in 2025. A sample of 61 auditors across 13 KAPs was gathered using non-probability sampling (convenience and snowball sampling). Data analysis was performed using Partial Least Squares - Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) with SmartPLS 4.0. The findings reveal that auditor integrity and competence have a positive and significant effect on audit quality. Conversely, auditor independence does not significantly affect audit quality. Furthermore, audit client retention does not significantly moderate the relationships between independence, integrity, or competence and audit quality. These findings highlight the need for accounting firms and regulators to emphasize reinforcing auditor integrity and competence to sustain and improve audit quality.

latest.title: When Pixels Persuade: Virtual Influencer Content Appeals, Credibility, and Generation Z Purchase Intention
latest.abstract: This study investigates how the emotional, rational and authenticity appeals of virtual influencer (VI) content, together with VI credibility, shape Generation Z purchase intention through perceived content value and consumer engagement. An online survey was conducted among Indonesian Generation Z Instagram users who had been exposed to Lil Miquela’s Calvin Klein content, and the proposed model was estimated using partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM). The results reveal that rational appeal, emotional appeal and VI credibility are positively associated with perceived content value, whereas authenticity appeal shows no significant relationship. Perceived content value is positively related to consumer engagement, which in turn is positively related to purchase intention. Perceived content value mediates the relationships of rational appeal, emotional appeal and VI credibility with engagement, and engagement mediates the link between perceived content value and purchase intention. The study extends advertising value and source credibility perspectives to non-human endorsers by demonstrating that message characteristics and source evaluations operate jointly in VI marketing. For practitioners, the findings highlight the importance of informative, emotionally relevant and credible VI content. The cross-sectional, single-influencer and single-brand design limits causal inference and generalisability.

latest.title: Peran Financial self-efficacy dalam Memoderasi Literasi Keuangan Digital, Herding behavior, dan Perilaku Keuangan Mahasiswa
latest.abstract: This study aims to analyze the influence of digital financial literacy and herding behavior on financial behavior, as well as to examine the role of financial self-efficacy as a moderating variable. The study sample consisted of economics education students from State University of Malang and State University of Surabaya. Data were collected using questionnaires. A quantitative approach was employed, utilizing multiple linear regression and Moderated Regression Analysis (MRA). The results indicate that digital financial literacy has a positive and significant effect on financial behavior, whereas herding behavior has a negative and significant effect. Moderation analysis reveals that financial self-efficacy strengthens the impact of digital financial literacy on financial behavior and weakens the impact of herding behavior on financial behavior. These findings suggest that enhancing digital financial literacy can foster better financial behavior, while the tendency to follow others' financial decisions can diminish the quality of financial behavior.

latest.title: Strategic Branding and Product Line Extension: Developing tentangKita's Personality Series
latest.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
latest.abstract: Abstract This paper presents a strategic branding and product line extension plan for tentangKita, an Indonesian conversation-based brand dedicated to fostering meaningful communication and deeper interpersonal connections. The project focuses on developing a new product line, Personality Series: The MBTI Couples Collection, which extends tentangKita’s existing conversation card offerings into a personality-based collection designed specifically for romantic partners. The proposed product line consists of 16 MBTI-inspired editions, each designed to transform personality exploration into engaging and meaningful conversations between couples. By incorporating personality-based themes into the brand’s established conversation card category, the extension aims to provide a differentiated product experience while maintaining consistency with tentangKita’s existing brand identity and purpose. The strategic development encompasses brand positioning, consumer insights, target audience identification, product differentiation, brand identity, and integrated marketing communication. The communication strategy incorporates digital campaigns, social media engagement, influencer collaborations, community activation, and experiential marketing to introduce the new collection and strengthen consumer engagement. The project is guided by the central idea of deeper understanding, positioning the Personality Series as more than a personality-themed card game. Instead, it serves as a conversation tool that encourages couples to explore individual differences, improve communication, and develop stronger emotional connections. Ultimately, this product line extension seeks to strengthen tentangKita’s brand relevance, expand its appeal within the romantic relationship segment, and create new op

latest.title: YouTube Influencer Marketing and Consumer Behavior : A Bibliometric Analysis
latest.abstract: Purpose : The purpose of this study was to map the intellectual structure of research on YouTube influencer marketing and consumer behavior from 2009 to 2025 by conducting performance analysis and science mapping using a bibliometric analysis methodology and proposed directions for future research. Design/Methodology/Approach : The authors used VOSviewer and Biblioshiny scientific tools to conduct the analyses. The study employed a bibliometric analysis of 86 documents that were retrieved from the Scopus database along with using a structured keyword search strategy and database filters. Findings : We found that research publications in this domain of research fluctuated during the study period, with the highest annual publications, which were 19 recorded in 2024. We also identified 38 keywords grouped into seven clusters in keyword co-occurrence analysis which covered YouTube-based influencer marketing, consumer behavior and purchase intention, social media marketing and branding, influencer credibility and parasocial relationships, information quality, digital creator formats, and social influence. Practical Implications : This study provided valuable insights for researchers, policymakers, academicians, companies, and brands to understand the knowledge structure of YouTube influencer marketing and its relationship with consumer behavior. Originality/Value : This study showed a platform - specific bibliometric overview of YouTube influencer marketing and consumer behavior by mapping the intellectual structure and identifying new directions for future research.

latest.title: The Psychological Mechanisms of Scarcity Marketing on Gen Z Impulse Buying Behavior in Malaysia: A Conceptual Framework
latest.abstract: Scarcity marketing has become a dominant persuasive strategy in digital retail, yet its psychological impact on Generation Z consumers in Malaysia remains underexplored. This concept paper proposes a conceptual framework examining the psychological mechanisms through which scarcity marketing influences impulse buying behavior among Malaysian Gen Z consumers. Grounded in the Stimulus-Organism-Response (S-O-R) framework and integrating Commodity Theory and Social Comparison Theory, the framework posits that three scarcity marketing stimuli—time-limited, quantity-limited, and social proof scarcity—activate four psychological mediators: fear of missing out (FOMO), competitive arousal, perceived urgency, and social comparison, which subsequently drive impulse buying behavior. The framework further proposes that self-control, digital literacy, financial literacy, and brand trust moderate these relationships. Drawing upon a systematic review of literature from 2017 to 2026, this paper synthesizes empirical evidence demonstrating that FOMO exerts the strongest mediating influence on impulse buying, while self-control consistently weakens the relationship between psychological mediators and behavioral outcomes. The proposed framework contributes to consumer behavior theory by clarifying the mediating pathways and boundary conditions of scarcity marketing effects and offers practical implications for marketers, policymakers and consumer educators in developing responsible marketing practices and targeted digital literacy interventions. Empirical validation through quantitative survey methods targeting 400 Malaysian Gen Z consumers aged 18–27 is proposed to test the hypothesized relationships using Structural Equation Modelling.

latest.title: Values in passenger narratives: is value-related expression associated with air passenger satisfaction?
Religious sensitivity in controversial advertising: A comparative study of consumer behavior in Pakistan and Hungary
latest.abstract: Building on Cognitive Appraisal Theory, this study examines the impact of controversial advertisements on consumer emotions and behaviors, with a particular focus on the moderating effect of religiosity. A study based on two countries, Pakistan (N = 320) and Hungary (N = 305), reveals that perceived controversial advertising significantly and positively predicts adverse word of mouth and ad avoidance in both countries. Customer outrage mediates these relationships, serving as an emotional mechanism that drives negative consumer out comes. Additionally, religiosity moderates the relationship between controversial advertising and customer outrage, with higher religiosity levels intensifying negative reactions. These findings underscore the importance of emotional and cultural factors in advertising strategies. By highlighting the dual role of customer outrage and religiosity, this research contributes to the literature on controversial advertising and offers practical insights for marketers aiming to navigate the potential risks of backlash.

latest.title: Product quality and price alongside physical evidence in Hanasui lipstick purchase intention
latest.abstract: This study examines associations of perceived product quality, price, and physical evidence with intention to purchase Hanasui lipstick at Toko Kawan Skincare, North Sumatra. The source study used a convenience sample of 96 repeat store customers, including 64 civil servants. Recruitment and eligibility verification were insufficiently documented. Reported OLS summaries gave F(3, 92) = 161.50, p < .001, and R² = .840. Product quality (B = 0.332, 95% CI [0.167, 0.497]), price perception (B = 0.187, 95% CI [0.012, 0.362]), and physical evidence (B = 0.417, 95% CI [0.169, 0.665]) had positive conditional associations. Their unique increments in R² were approximately .028, .008, and .019. VIFs of 4.433-6.856, overlapping and double-barreled items, and a Durbin-Watson statistic of .841 limit interpretation. The latter raises a concern about residual dependence in the recorded order but does not establish recruitment clustering. Conventional inference remains provisional because respondent-level data and recruitment metadata were unavailable for robustness checks. A regression sensitivity analysis gives an 80%-power benchmark of f² ≈ .0835 for one coefficient under independent errors. Physical evidence as trial infrastructure is proposed as a category-specific extension of servicescape reasoning, not an empirically tested mechanism: trial use, perceived risk, and need for touch were not measured. The findings do not establish a ranking of managerial priorities or justify prioritizing facilities over pricing.

latest.title: Effect of Supply Chain Risk Management on Operational Performance of Raising the Village in Gasabo District, Rwanda
latest.venue: Journal of Research Innovation and Implications in Education
latest.abstract: The purpose of this study was to examine the effect of Supply Chain Risk Management on Operational Performance of Raising the Village in Gasabo District, Rwanda.The study was guided by four specific objectives, namely, to assess the effect of Supplier Risk Management, Inventory Risk Management, Transportation & Logistics Risk Management, and Information & Technology Risk Management on Operational Performance.The target population was 219 employees and stakeholders connected to Raising the Village operations in Gasabo District, while a sample size of 142 respondents was calculated using Slovin's formula.Quantitative data were processed through editing, coding, and tabulation, and analysis was performed using SPSS Version 29 through descriptive statistics, correlation analysis, and multiple regression analysis.A total of 136 complete questionnaires (95.8%) were analysed.The regression findings indicated that Supplier Risk Management B = 0.163, t = 3.396, p = 0.001, Inventory Risk Management B = 0.142, t = 2.679, p = 0.008, Transportation and Logistics Risk Management B = 0.389, t = 7.073, p = 0.000, Information and Technology Risk Management B = 0.171, t = 3.288, p = 0.001 had positive and statistically significant effects on Operational Performance in Raising the Village in Gasabo District, Rwanda.The study concluded that strengthening Supplier Risk Management, Inventory Risk Management, Transportation and Logistics Risk Management, Information and Technology Risk Management improve Operational Performance.It is recommended that management should strengthen the most influential practices while maintaining continuous monitoring of all significant variables.

latest.title: Marketing Communication Strategy Through Social Media Content based on Local Wisdom to Increase the Added Value of Indonesian Coffee Brands (Study on Conservation Coffee Brands Based on Local Wisdom)
latest.abstract: The coffee industry is a significant sector in Indonesia, contributing to both domestic production and consumption. However, challenges such as declining production due to climate change, limited agricultural land, and increasing global competition have encouraged coffee businesses to adopt more innovative marketing strategies. One emerging approach involves social media marketing communications that incorporate local cultural values and traditional knowledge. This study aimed to explore the social media marketing communication strategies employed by Indonesian coffee businesses, particularly those incorporating local wisdom, and examine their implications for brand value. A descriptive qualitative approach employing a holistic single-case study design was adopted. Data were collected through semi-structured interviews with consumers and coffee business owners who actively incorporated local wisdom-based content into their marketing strategies. The findings indicated that such content fostered emotional connections with consumers, enhanced brand awareness and engagement, and strengthened brand loyalty. These findings highlight the strategic potential of integrating local cultural values into social media marketing communications to enhance brand differentiation, strengthen perceived brand value, and support long-term business sustainability in Indonesia's coffee industry

latest.title: Artificial Intelligence in Social Media Marketing in Bangladesh: Business Practices, Consumer Perceptions and Challenges
latest.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is changing social media marketing by helping businesses create content, target audiences, improve customer engagement and optimize advertising campaigns. However, its growing use also raises concerns about data privacy, transparency and consumer trust. This qualitative study explores how businesses and marketers in Bangladesh experience AI in social media marketing, which adoption barriers they face and how consumers perceive AI-driven personalized marketing. Using purposive sampling, 45 semi-structured in-depth interviews were conducted, of which 30 complete interviews were retained, and ten interviews were analyzed in depth through thematic analysis guided by the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM) and consumer trust and privacy perspectives. The analysis identified six themes: AI-enabled content creation and operational efficiency; personalized targeting and advertising optimization; analytics, customer insight and trend identification; automated customer engagement; privacy, accuracy and ethical concerns; and human judgement, skills and contextual adoption challenges. Business respondents generally reported conditional trust in AI, whereas consumer respondents reported low trust and a strong preference for transparency, consent and control over their data. Tentative differences between smaller and larger firms are also discussed. The study contributes to understanding AI-driven social media marketing in Bangladesh by placing business and consumer perspectives side by side and by extending TAM with trust and privacy considerations. Its findings may help businesses develop more effective and responsible marketing strategies and support policy attention to transparency, data protection and consumer confidence.

latest.title: How do customers react to preferential treatment? An affective events theory and time-lagged survey
latest.abstract: Understanding how preferential treatment influences customer behavior is pivotal in shaping effective marketing strategies. This study looks at how customers feel and act when they get special treatment compared to others (preferential treatment), using the idea of how emotions are stirred by certain events to understand its effect on what customers do (affective events theory). Using a time-lagged survey of 318 customers in the retail sector, we explored how preferential treatment influences three kinds of customer behavior: feeling extremely happy (customer delight), speaking favorably about a product or service (customer advocacy), and making unplanned purchases (impulse buying). We discovered that preferential treatment makes customers much happier, which then encourages them to both advocate for and buy products on a whim. Unexpectedly, our findings indicate that preferential treatment’s ability to elevate customer happiness is somewhat diminished in those with a higher inclination toward seeking attention (attention-seeking motives), due to a perceived lack of genuineness or merit in the treatment received. Consequently, this study illustrates the complex dynamics of preferential treatment in enhancing customer delight, advocacy, and impulse purchasing, while also uncovering the noteworthy role of individual differences in these processes.

latest.title: Business location, product quality and electronic word of mouth in bakery purchase decisions in Kisaran, North Sumatra
latest.abstract: This study examines the reported associations of business location, product quality, and electronic word of mouth (e-WOM) with purchase decisions among 96 customers of Zahra Bakery and Cake Shop in Kisaran, Indonesia. The source study used non-probability sampling, but recruitment details and respondent profiles are unavailable. This article audits aggregate regression summaries; it does not reanalyze respondent-level data. The reported model summary gives F(3, 92) = 103.06, p < .001, and R² = .771. Using the coefficient-table standard errors, location has the largest reconstructed unique association (B = 0.692, 95% CI [0.595, 0.789], f² = 2.168), followed by quality (B = 0.392, 95% CI [0.293, 0.491], f² = 0.668) and e-WOM (B = 0.272, 95% CI [0.157, 0.387], f² = 0.239). Conflicting partial-test statistics produce substantially different effect sizes; however, residual assumptions remain unverified. Quality items P7 and P8 have item-total correlations of .041 and .035, while location's alpha of .966 raises a concern about item redundancy. These issues prevent a definitive comparison of predictor importance. A proximity-first account is proposed as a hypothesis for future testing, because travel time, purchase frequency, first-time versus repeat purchases, and purchase occasions were not measured. The contribution is a context-specific, provisional account of scale-score associations and a transparent arithmetic audit, rather than empirical confirmation of the proposed mechanisms.

latest.title: Prospects of Rural Tourism in Sustainable Territorial Management in Uzbekistan
latest.venue: American Journal of Economics and Business Management
latest.abstract: This article proposes some solutions for optimising the rural areas management and making better use of tourism opportunities to ensure sustainable development. It also analyses the situation of family tourism stakeholders in rural areas of Uzbekistan and makes predictions about how they may affect the economic development of rural areas. These forecasts, known as regression, transformation and synergy effects, show in concrete case studies how the decisions of family businesses affect the development of tourism in rural areas. Based on the experiences of the rural families who participated in the study, the concept of a “tourism frontier” of the tourism business is proposed, highlighting the important aspects that should be taken into account when using rural life as a tourism resource. In addition, the article presents theoretical views on rural tourism resources and reveals specific aspects of the approach to rural tourism management in the conditions of Uzbekistan. Thus, the research results of the article provide a better understanding of the tourism enterprises in rural areas and the mechanisms of interaction with the external and internal environment.

latest.title: Bridging Channels, Building Loyalty : The Role of Customer Satisfaction in Omnichannel Integration
latest.abstract: Purpose : This paper aimed to investigate the relationship between channel integration (CI) and customer loyalty in the context of an omnichannel environment, while examining the mediating role of customer satisfaction. The study validated established relationships in an omnichannel marketing environment. Design/Methodology/Approach : The current study used a quantitative research design wherein data were obtained through a structured questionnaire using a 5-point Likert scale. Data were collected from 450 respondents who used JioMart’s omnichannel services in South Odisha and analyzed using structural equation modeling (SEM). Findings : The current study investigated the relationships between CI, customer satisfaction, and customer loyalty in an omnichannel marketing environment by means of SEM. The findings showed that CI had a positive impact on customer satisfaction and loyalty. Customer satisfaction resulted in greater loyalty. Furthermore, satisfaction partially mediated the relationship between CI and loyalty, suggesting that integration influenced loyalty predominantly through customer satisfaction. Practical Implications : It was deemed important that managers focus on CI to improve customer satisfaction, which in turn could develop their loyalty toward a particular brand. It appeared essential that a seamless experience could be provided to customers through holistic integration of channels. As CI influenced loyalty both directly and, more strongly, through customer satisfaction, businesses need to integrate technology to strengthen both pathways. Originality/Value : The paper made a valuable contribution to the body of knowledge as it empirically tested the mediating effect of customer satisfaction on the relationship between CI and customer loyalty.

latest.title: Influence of Chatbots on Consumer Purchase Decision-Making in Luxury Products
latest.venue: International Journal of Modern Science and Research Technology
latest.abstract: The rapid introduction of artificial intelligence into digital commerce has altered the way brands interact with their customers, particularly in the luxury sector, where personal contact and exclusivity are essential for adding value. Among the different technologies, chatbots have emerged as important tools since they allow for immediate communication, recommend products, and offer personalized help. This study examines how consumers view chatbots in the context of luxury products and develops a conceptual framework that links the features of chatbots – specifically responsiveness, personalization, anthropomorphism, and interactivity – with customers' intention to make a purchase through the intermediary effects of trust, perceived value, and emotional engagement. Unlike in the case of mass-market buying, luxury consumption is rooted in symbolic value, in the demonstration of status, and in the satisfaction obtained from the experience rather than simply in functionality, so the character of the digital interaction becomes particularly significant. An exploratory quantitative approach is used in the study, with a survey carried out of people who have used chatbot services on luxury websites. A Chi-square test of independence reveals a statistically significant relationship between the perception of chatbot design (to the extent that it appeared robotic) and the perception of ease of navigation, indicating that opinions about design and usability are related rather than independent. Since the sample size is small, this result is regarded as exploratory and indicative rather than conclusive, and the proposed connections between personalization, responsiveness, trust, perceived value, and purchase intention are given as a conceptual framework for future empirical researc

latest.title: Workload, work stress, and work environment as predictors of self-rated employee performance in Asahan Regency
latest.abstract: This study examines the associations between reported workload, work stress, and the work environment and self-rated employee performance at the Asahan Regency Population and Civil Registration Office, Indonesia. A cross-sectional census surveyed all 70 employees in February 2026. The reported OLS model explained 47.1% of the performance-score variance, F(3, 66) = 19.58, p < .001. The workload composite was positively associated with performance (B = 0.387, reported 95% CI [0.244, 0.530], β = .576, p < .001). Work stress (B = -0.010, CI [-0.216, 0.196], p = .924) and the work environment (B = 0.190, CI [-0.042, 0.422], p = .107) were not statistically significant; these findings do not establish an absence of association. Interpretation is limited because workload items combine demands, fatigue, fatigue-related errors, and productivity, while stress items include workload and environmental conditions. The workload coefficient therefore does not isolate the association of workload demands with performance. Challenge appraisal, assignment of more tasks to employees perceived as capable, and overlapping item content are alternative explanations, none of which were directly tested. Item-level responses and the complete administered questionnaire were unavailable for this revision, preventing exclusion of the productivity item and re-estimation of the model. The contribution is contextual evidence about reported score associations and a framework for separating demand, assignment, strain, and performance in future research. The findings do not justify increasing workloads or dismissing stress and workplace conditions.
latest.subfield: Organizational Behavior and Human Resource Management

latest.title: Compensating for the past or shaping the future: how raw materials in green products impact consumers’ purchase intentions
latest.venue: Asia Pacific Journal of Marketing and Logistics
latest.abstract: Purpose This study investigates how different types of raw materials (virgin eco-friendly vs recycled) used to make green products interact with consumers’ regulatory focus to influence their purchase intentions. Design/methodology/approach We conduct two experiments using a between-subjects design to examine the interaction effect of raw material type and consumers’ regulatory focus on purchase intentions, as well as the mediating mechanism of perceived consumer effectiveness. Findings Our results show that promotion-focused consumers have stronger purchase intentions for green products made with virgin eco-friendly materials, whereas prevention-focused consumers exhibit stronger purchase intentions for products made with recycled materials. This effect is partially mediated by perceived consumer effectiveness. Originality/value This study links consumers’ regulatory focus with green product raw material types and identifies conditions that reduce consumer resistance to recycled products, offering new insights for designing and marketing green products.

latest.title: Digital Marketing Transformation in Tourism: The Effectiveness of Social Media Promotion Strategies in Attracting Millennials to Agrotourism Destinations in Baubau City
latest.venue: Journal of Mathematics Instruction Social Research and Opinion
latest.abstract: Digital transformation in tourism has had a major influence on promotional strategies, especially those targeting millennial tourists. This study aims to (1) analyze the implementation of digital marketing transformation in the promotion of agrotourism destinations; (2) analyze the effectiveness of social media as a promotional tool for attracting the interest of millennials in agrotourism destinations; and (3) analyze the influence of promotional strategies, in terms of content types and social media platforms, on millennials' interest in visiting agrotourism destinations. Using a mixed-methods design that combined qualitative and quantitative descriptive approaches, data were collected through questionnaires and in-depth interviews with 35 respondents, including tourism managers and tourists, as well as through social media content analysis and surveys. The qualitative data were analyzed using Miles and Huberman's interactive model, which comprises data reduction, data presentation, and conclusion drawing. The quantitative data were analyzed using multiple linear regression. The results show that Betoambari's digital marketing transformation has effectively supported promotion and increased millennials' interest in visiting. The promotion's success was mainly driven by the destination's attractiveness, strengthened through visual content, digital interaction, and user-generated content on social media. Social media, particularly Facebook and YouTube, plays a significant role in attracting millennial tourists to agrotourism destinations. Attractive visual content, digital interaction through comments and likes, and user-generated content such as reviews and recommendations have proven effective in increasing visits. The regression results show that the model explains 9

latest.title: Artificial Intelligence and Consumer Purchase Behavior: A Bibliometric Analysis of Research Trends and Emerging Directions
latest.abstract: This study maps the academic research landscape on artificial intelligence (AI) and consumer purchase through a bibliometric analysis of Scopus-indexed journal articles from 2020 to 2025. A structured search of titles, abstracts and keywords in Scopus yielded 343 journal articles after excluding conference proceedings, book chapters and other source types. We examined the corpus along five dimensions: document and source types, the evolution of published studies since 2020, the distribution of subject areas, keyword co-occurrence, and citation metrics for highly cited articles. The publication output grew gradually from 2020 to 2023 and increased significantly from 2024 onwards, with 2025 recording the highest number of publications. This growth coincides with the mainstreaming of conversational AI and the advent of generative AI. The field is interdisciplinary, spanning business and management, computer science, the social sciences, psychology and decision sciences. Keyword co-occurrence analysis indicates that purchase intention, consumer behavior, marketing and sales are the conceptual anchors and the most cited articles focus on technology acceptance, trust, chatbot purchase intention, virtual influencer marketing and environmental sustainability. This study provides a quantitative map of the literature on AI and consumer purchase for 2020-2025 and highlights the dominant role of trust and perceived value in the literature, as well as open questions about long-term effects and cross-cultural generalizability.

latest.title: Cognitive networks reconstruct mindsets about STEM subjects and educational contexts in high-schoolers, undergraduates, experts and their digital twins
latest.abstract: Attitudes toward STEM develop from the interaction of conceptual knowledge, educational experiences, and affect. Here we use cognitive network science to reconstruct group mindsets as behavioural forma mentis networks (BFMNs). In this case, nodes are cue words and free associations, edges are empirical associative links, and each concept is annotated with perceived valence. We analyse BFMNs from $$N=981$$ observations spanning high school students, university students, and early-career STEM experts, alongside LLM (GPT-OSS) “digital twins” (group-level synthetic counterparts, not individual-level copies), prompted to emulate comparable profiles. Focusing also on semantic neighbourhoods (“frames”) around key target concepts (e.g., STEM subjects or educational actors/places), we quantify frames in terms of valence auras, emotional profiles, network overlap (Jaccard similarity), and concreteness relative to null baselines. Across student groups, science and research are consistently framed positively, while their core quantitative subjects (mathematics and statistics) exhibit more negative and anxiety-related auras, amplified in higher math-anxiety subgroups, evidencing a STEM-science cognitive and emotional dissonance. High-anxiety frames are also less concrete than chance, suggesting more abstract and decontextualised representations of threatening quantitative domains. Human networks show greater overlap between mathematics and anxiety than GPT-OSS. The results highlight how BFMNs capture cognitive-affective signatures of mindsets towards the target domains and indicate that these synthetic counterparts approximate cultural attitudes but miss key context-sensitive, experience-based components of human educational anxiety.

latest.title: Social Commerce Adoption and MSME Marketing Performance: The Mediating Role of Digital Trust and the Moderating Role of Digital Literacy
latest.abstract: Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menganalisis pengaruh adopsi social commerce terhadap kinerja pemasaran UMKM melalui peran mediasi kepercayaan digital, serta menguji peran moderasi literasi digital pada hubungan antara adopsi social commerce dan kepercayaan digital. Penelitian ini menggunakan pendekatan kuantitatif dengan populasi UMKM sektor kuliner, fesyen, dan kerajinan di Kota Surakarta yang telah mengadopsi social commerce. Sampel ditentukan menggunakan teknik purposive sampling dengan jumlah 150 responden UMKM. Data dianalisis menggunakan Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) melalui perangkat lunak SmartPLS. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa adopsi social commerce berpengaruh positif dan signifikan terhadap kinerja pemasaran UMKM maupun terhadap kepercayaan digital, kepercayaan digital berpengaruh positif dan signifikan terhadap kinerja pemasaran UMKM, serta kepercayaan digital terbukti memediasi secara parsial pengaruh adopsi social commerce terhadap kinerja pemasaran UMKM. Namun, literasi digital tidak terbukti memoderasi pengaruh adopsi social commerce terhadap kepercayaan digital. Penelitian ini memberikan kontribusi teoritis melalui penerapan kerangka Stimulus-Organism-Response pada konteks transformasi digital UMKM, serta implikasi praktis bahwa penguatan kepercayaan digital merupakan strategi kunci bagi UMKM dalam mengoptimalkan manfaat social commerce, sementara literasi digital lebih berperan sebagai prediktor langsung dibandingkan faktor penguat.

latest.title: Controlling Differently: Internal Control Digitalization as a Dynamic Capability. A Conceptual Framework and Research Propositions
latest.venue: Revue Internationale des Sciences de Gestion
latest.abstract: The digitalization of internal control is widely presented as a lever of performance, yet the mechanisms behind this contribution remain unclear. This article argues that the dominant readings of the phenomenon, whether technical, compliance-based, or resource-based, share a common assumption: they treat digitalization as a state rather than as an ability, which prevents them from explaining why comparable tools produce different outcomes and why well-performing control systems become obsolete. Drawing on an integrative literature review and a theory adaptation approach, the article reinterprets internal control digitalization through dynamic capabilities theory. It distinguishes technological resources, operational capabilities, and dynamic capabilities, and defines internal control digitalization as a capability combining continuous risk sensing, deliberate response, and ongoing reconfiguration of the control system. This reinterpretation uncovers a tension between reconfiguration and the stability on which control reliability rests, and introduces the concept of reconfiguration governance, which is distinguished from IT change management and structured around five dimensions. Six propositions follow. The capability affects organizational performance mainly through two parallel and partial mediators, risk management effectiveness and internal control reliability, provided that data are of adequate quality and that automated controls remain under human oversight. Reconfiguration governance determines whether the capability strengthens or weakens control reliability, environmental dynamism moderates the relationship in an inverted U-shaped manner, and institutional pressures weaken it only when they lead to symbolic adoption. The article confronts these propositions wit

latest.title: The Role of Customer Satisfaction In Mediating The Effect of Service Performance and Perceived Value On Customer Loyalty: Evidence From A B2B Outsourced Cleaning Service In A Pharmaceutical Manufacturing Setting
latest.venue: International Journal of Educational Research & Social Sciences
latest.abstract: Outsourced facility services have become a strategic component of operations in Indonesia's highly regulated pharmaceutical industry, where cleanliness is not a cosmetic concern but a compliance requirement embedded in CPOB, WHO Prequalification, ISO 9001:2015, and ISO 14001:2015 standards. This study examined why an outsourced cleaning-service provider operating exclusively for a single pharmaceutical client since 2013 recorded 38 client complaints between November 2025 and January 2026, of which 66% concerned Service Performance and Perceived Value, and asked whether Customer Satisfaction mediates the effects of these two constructs on Customer Loyalty. Prior research has largely tested this chain in consumer-facing settings, leaving the business-to-business, compliance-driven pharmaceutical outsourcing context empirically unexamined. A quantitative, explanatory cross-sectional survey collected primary data from 355 employees of PT Bio Farma (Persero) Pasteur, Bandung, drawn by simple random sampling from a population of 3,096 and analyzed using PLS-SEM in SmartPLS. All eight hypotheses were supported at the 5% significance level. The model explained 74.0% of the variance in Customer Satisfaction and 68.3% of the variance in Customer Loyalty. Service Performance showed the strongest association with Customer Satisfaction (β = 0.543; f² = 0.901), while Customer Satisfaction showed the strongest association with Customer Loyalty (β = 0.494) and partially mediated both upstream paths (indirect effects β = 0.269 and β = 0.229). The study empirically extends the satisfaction-mediation framework to regulated B2B outsourcing and indicates that satisfaction management should be the central lever in loyalty-building strategy.

latest.title: Perancangan Booklet sebagai Media Promosi Wisata Edukasi Susu di Desa Padusan, Kabupaten Mojokerto
latest.venue: KOMUNITA Jurnal Pengabdian dan Pemberdayaan Masyarakat
latest.abstract: Desa Padusan, Kabupaten Mojokerto, memiliki potensi wisata edukasi berbasis pengolahan susu, tetapi potensi tersebut belum didukung oleh media promosi yang terintegrasi dan menarik secara visual. Program pengabdian kepada masyarakat ini bertujuan merancang booklet sebagai media edukasi dan promosi wisata pengolahan susu di Padusan. Program menggunakan pendekatan Design Thinking melalui lima tahap: Empathize, Define, Ideate, Prototype, dan Testing. Identifikasi kebutuhan dan evaluasi produk dilakukan melalui wawancara dan diskusi dengan Dinas Pariwisata dan Kebudayaan setempat serta kuesioner kepada responden masyarakat. Luaran berupa booklet 10 halaman yang menyajikan perawatan sapi perah, pemerahan, pengecekan mutu susu, pengemasan dan pemasaran, serta produk olahan susu. Pengujian kepada 40 responden dan evaluasi Dinas Pariwisata dan Kebudayaan menunjukkan bahwa booklet dinilai informatif, menarik, mudah dipahami, dan relevan dengan promosi wisata saat ini. Responden berasal dari kelompok usia yang beragam dengan dominasi Generasi Z. Booklet juga memenuhi kriteria evaluasi SMART dan berpotensi menjadi media promosi praktis untuk mendukung wisata edukasi dan kuliner di Desa Padusan.Booklet; Promosi Pariwisata; Wisata Edukasi; Pengolahan Susu; Design Thinking

latest.title: The Effect of Campus Image and Word of Mouth on Students' Decisions in Choosing a Business Education Study Program at State University Of Medan
latest.venue: Jurnal Ilmiah Ekonomi, Manajemen dan Bisnis
latest.abstract: This study aims to analyze the influence of campus image and word of mouth on the decision of 2025 cohort students in choosing the Business Education Study Program at Universitas Negeri Medan. This research employed a quantitative approach using an ex post facto method. The population consisted of 111 students, all of whom were selected as the sample through the total sampling technique. Data were collected using a Likert-scale questionnaire and analyzed using multiple linear regression, t-test, F-test, and the coefficient of determination (R²). The results showed that campus image had a positive and significant influence on students' decisions in choosing the Business Education Study Program at Medan State University (t value = 7.322; sig = 0.000 < 0.05). Word of mouth also had a positive and significant influence on students' decisions in choosing the Business Education Study Program at Medan State University (t value = 5.779; sig = 0.000 < 0.05). Simultaneously, both variables had a positive and significant influence on students' decisions in choosing the Business Education Study Program at Medan State University (f value = 40.939; sig = 0.000 < 0.05). The findings indicate that 43.1% of the variation in students' decisions to choose the Business Education Study Program can be explained by campus image and word of mouth, while the remaining 56.9% is influenced by other factors outside the scope of this study.

latest.title: Transformation of Business Communication Model in Crisis: Rebranding of Warung New Bahari into Ekspresss Bahari
latest.venue: Journal of Asian Multicultural Research for Economy and Management Study
latest.abstract: This study examines the transformation of the business communication model in the franchise crisis experienced by Warung New Bahari (WNB), which underwent rebranding into Ekspresss Bahari (WEB) and succeeded in maintaining only 30 of 125 outlets in the Jabodetabek region. Using a qualitative approach with a case study design, data were collected through in-depth interviews with 12 informants, participatory observation of 8 outlets, business document analysis, and two focus group discussions. Findings reveal that there is a structural disjunction between the implementation of Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) technology and the Cultural Intelligence (CQ) of organizational actors, manifested in seven forms of communication gaps. The transformation of the communication model was designed through three phases—restart-up, reconcept, and rebranding—by integrating CQ into every layer of business communication. The recommended communication model integrates ERP as a strategic communication platform, CQ as the core competence of organizational actors, and Artificial Intelligence (AI) as an operational enabler. The novelty of this research lies in bridging the studies of ERP, business communication, and cultural intelligence in the context of crisis, downsizing, and rebranding of franchise-based MSMEs.

latest.title: Bank complaint resolution outcomes and customer behavioural biases for accountable financial institutions in guwahati India
latest.venue: International Journal of Marketing Research Innovation
latest.abstract: Customer complaints against banks in India have risen sharply with the spread of digital banking, and accountable and transparent grievance redressal has become central to consumer protection and strong institutions. Earlier studies linked complaint handling to satisfaction and loyalty but paid little attention to how the outcome of a resolved complaint shapes the customer's later judgement. This study examines the influence of bank complaint resolution outcomes on four post-resolution behavioural biases: confirmation bias, loss aversion, overconfidence and complaint avoidance. Primary data were collected through a cross-sectional survey using a structured questionnaire from 547 customers across 329 branches of 12 public- and 12 private-sector banks in Guwahati City, India, who had lodged a formal complaint and were analysed using descriptive statistics, Cronbach's alpha and simple linear regression. The results show that 56.3% of complaints were fully resolved, 40.0% partially resolved, and 3.7% not resolved, and that the bias scales were reliable (α = 0.781 to 0.893). Complaint resolution outcome was positively related to confirmation bias (β = 0.764, R² = 0.584), loss aversion (β = 0.808, R² = 0.652) and overconfidence (β = 0.663, R² = 0.440), and negatively related to complaint avoidance (β = −0.783, R² = 0.613), all at p < 0.001. Loss aversion recorded the highest mean score (3.88) and confirmation bias the lowest (2.68). The findings suggest that complaint resolution outcomes account for 44.0% to 65.2% of the variation in post-resolution behavioural biases, indicating that resolving a complaint is a behavioural event, not just a procedural closure, within inclusive financial services. JEL Classification Codes: G21, G41, D18, D91, M31.

latest.title: Brand Image Sebagai Variabel Mediasi Bauran Pemasaran dan Lifestyle Terhadap Keputusan Pembelian
latest.venue: Jurnal Akuntansi Ekonomi dan Manajemen Bisnis
latest.abstract: This study aims to examine the influence of the marketing mix (product quality, price, and promotion) and lifestyle on purchasing decisions for Apple smartphones in Samarinda City, with brand image serving as a mediating variable. Using a quantitative explanatory approach, data were collected from 145 Apple smartphone users in Samarinda. Data analysis was conducted using Partial Least Squares (PLS). The findings indicate that product quality, promotion, and lifestyle have a positive and significant effect on brand image as well as on purchasing decisions, both directly and indirectly. However, price was found to have no significant effect on brand image. This finding suggests that Apple consumers in Samarinda perceive price as a logical consequence of a premium product rather than as a primary factor in shaping brand image. Therefore, strengthening the lifestyle ecosystem appears to be more effective than merely adjusting pricing strategies. Future research is recommended to expand the framework by incorporating additional variables in order to provide a deeper analysis of the factors driving consumer purchasing decisions.

latest.title: Fear of Missing Out and Hyperconnectivity: An Empirical Economic Study on African SMEs
latest.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
latest.abstract: Abstract: This article examines the role of Fear of Missing Out (FOMO) as a growth lever for African SMEs. Using ANSD data and sectoral reports, a multiple linear regression model integrates five variables: digitalization, AI adoption and penetration, Internet connectivity, and social media usage. Results show that internet (53.9%) and social media (28.8%) together explain over 80% of FOMO intensity, highlighting their central role in impulsive consumer behavior. Digitalization contributes secondarily, while AI remains marginal yet strategic. A comparison across Senegal, Nigeria, Kenya, and Ghana reveals a pan-African dynamic. Keywords: FOMO, Consumer, Supply Analysis, Modern Marketing, Risk JEL Classification Number: D3, D11, M31, G32

latest.title: Contextual institutional constraints and gender entrepreneurship in rural contexts
latest.venue: International Journal of Entrepreneurial Behaviour & Research
latest.abstract: Purpose This study explores the dual influence of contextual institutional constraints and gender entrepreneurship in rural contexts. Gender is applied as a critical lens to theorise entrepreneurship and its constraints (Ghouse and McElwee, 2026) in the gendered context (Welter, 2020) of rural family businesses. Design/methodology/approach From a dataset capturing the life stories of 30 entrepreneurs engaged in 22 rural family businesses, this work applies a gender lens and focuses on the life stories of 4 couples (men and women) owning and managing family businesses in rural Sweden. Following Larty and Hamilton (2011), the analysis structures the narratives of entrepreneurs in rural family businesses (cf. Alkhaled and Berglund, 2018) with the emerging themes of emancipation, empowerment and family business as an emancipatory space emerging as significant recurring themes in the stories of all four couples. Findings The findings reveal that rural family businesses provide women with a secure space that empowers and emancipates them to pursue entrepreneurial activities. Fathers play an important role in how daughters challenge traditional rural social norms, while contextual informal institutional constraints (i.e. traditional norms) hinder entrepreneurship in rural contexts. Here, the community acts as a vital stakeholder. Research limitations/implications This study challenges the assumptions of the heroic entrepreneur and the taken-for-granted agency of men. As such, in rural contexts, men act as co-agents to women entrepreneurs in pursuing entrepreneurship and emancipation. By including the voices of both women and men, this study responds to calls by scholars in the gender entrepreneurship literature (Smith, 2022; Hytti et al., 2024). Though empirical context is lim

latest.title: Do you prefer a familiar ride when you travel abroad? Tourism and cross-border M&A in the passenger transport sector
latest.abstract: This paper examines the relationship between tourism and cross-border mergers and acquisitions (M&A) in the passenger transport sector. We compile a novel dataset covering 81 countries over the period 1995–2019 and estimate a gravity model to assess whether M&A activity in this sector promotes or discourages bilateral tourism flows. In addition, we investigate whether the relationship between M&A and tourism is moderated by countries’ cultural distance and institutional quality. The results indicate that M&A activity is positively associated with bilateral tourism, and that this positive effect is stronger when cultural differences between countries are greater and when the destination country exhibits lower institutional quality. The positive association between M&A and tourism remains robust across a battery of tests designed to assess the causal nature of the relationship.

latest.title: Digital Transformation of Business Processes as a Factor in Increasing Competitiveness
latest.abstract: Purpose: This study examined the impact of business process digital transformation on the competitiveness of medium and large enterprises in Ukraine during 2021–2024. Design/Methodology/Approach: A quantitative panel econometric approach was applied using secondary financial and non-financial data for a balanced annual panel of 173 enterprises (692 observations). Integrated indices of digital transformation (five min–max normalised process indicators) and competitiveness (five z-standardised performance indicators) were constructed, and descriptive statistics, the Kolmogorov–Smirnov normality test, the Mann–Whitney U test for median-split groups, and, following the Hausman test, a fixed-effects regression with cluster-robust standard errors were employed. Research Limitations: The study was limited to medium and large Ukrainian enterprises and secondary data from 2021–2024. The estimates are associative rather than causal. Findings: Digitalisation increased steadily, competitiveness differed significantly across digitalisation levels, and the fixed-effects model showed a positive within-enterprise relationship between digital transformation and competitiveness. Higher digitalisation was associated with greater labour productivity, operating margins, revenue growth, and stronger market positions. Practical Implication: The findings support systematic digital modernisation as a strategy for improving enterprise competitiveness and can guide corporate digital strategies and policymaking. Social Implication: Business digitalisation may support organisational resilience, productivity, and sustainable economic development. Originality/Value: The study introduces the depth of digital integration of business processes as a variable, measured from enterprise reporting rather tha

latest.title: Financial Literacy and Financial Management Practices of Non-Teaching Employees in the Schools Division Office of the City of Ilagan
latest.venue: Student Journal of Technology and Educational Research
latest.abstract: This study examined the level of financial literacy and personal financial management practices among non-teaching employees and determined the relationships between the two variables. Financial literacy was assessed in terms of financial knowledge, financial skill, financial behavior, and financial self-efficacy, while personal financial management practices were examined through financial planning, financial management, income and asset protection, investment, analytical skills, budgeting, and financial acumen. Descriptive and correlational analyses were employed to describe the respondents' reported competencies and practices and determine the associations between the variables. The findings revealed that respondents demonstrated very high levels of financial literacy in all four dimensions, with grand means ranging from 3.49 to 3.54. Personal financial management practices were also rated very high in financial planning, financial management, income and asset protection, and investment, with grand means ranging from 3.52 to 3.63. However, analytical skills (2.55), budgeting (3.18), and financial acumen (2.87) received lower ratings, indicating areas for improvement. Correlational analysis showed that financial knowledge (r = .298), (p = .018) and financial self-efficacy (r = .282), (p = .026) were significantly and positively associated with financial planning. No statistically significant relationships were found between the other dimensions of financial literacy and personal financial management practices. The findings highlight the importance of strengthening practical financial competencies, particularly analytical skills, budgeting, and financial decision-making. Financial education programs incorporating practical exercises and goal-oriented activities may hel

hot.title: How generative AI Is shaping the future of marketing
hot.venue: Journal of the Academy of Marketing Science
hot.abstract: Abstract Generative AI (Gen AI) is shaping the future of marketing. In the next decade, Gen AI will influence how marketers interact and communicate with customers, help create and deliver marketing content (text, images, and video), and inform methods for researching and developing new products and services. In both service and sales settings, Gen AI will affect customers directly and significantly. Therefore, marketers, researchers, and public policy makers require a clear understanding of Gen AI and its potential, as well as its limitations. To assist marketers in thinking through the adoption and implementation of Gen AI, the current article presents a four-quadrant organizing framework that highlights trade-offs in both the nature of Gen AI inputs and the extent of human augmentation needed to deliver Gen AI–generated outputs. This framework provides guidance for the selection and implementation of Gen AI tools, as well as recommendations for further research.

hot.title: Artificial Intelligence and Its Role in Shaping Organizational Work Practices and Culture
hot.abstract: The advent of Artificial Intelligence (AI) is profoundly transforming organizational landscapes, significantly influencing work practices and triggering cultural shifts. This study explores the role of AI in reshaping organizational work practices and examines the resulting cultural transformation. Through a systematic literature review, this study synthesizes existing research to provide a comprehensive understanding of AI’s impact on organizational landscapes. A systematic literature review was conducted, analyzing peer-reviewed articles, books, and conference papers to identify key themes related to AI-driven changes in work practices, including automation, decision making, and employee roles. It also explores how these changes influence organizational culture, particularly shifts toward innovation, agility, and continuous learning, alongside challenges like resistance to change and ethical concerns. While AI adoption promises benefits such as enhanced efficiency, productivity, and innovation, it also presents significant challenges related to cultural alignment, employee resistance, ethical concerns, and leadership communication. Effective leadership, transparent communication, and investments in skills development emerge as pivotal strategies for overcoming these obstacles and ensuring successful AI implementation. The findings offer insights into the complex interplay between AI adoption and cultural transformation, highlighting gaps in the current research and suggesting directions for future studies. This study serves as a valuable resource for academics and practitioners seeking to understand the broader implications of AI on organizational structures and culture.
hot.subfield: Organizational Behavior and Human Resource Management

hot.title: The evolving field of digital mental health: current evidence and implementation issues for smartphone apps, generative artificial intelligence, and virtual reality
hot.abstract: The expanding domain of digital mental health is transitioning beyond traditional telehealth to incorporate smartphone apps, virtual reality, and generative artificial intelligence, including large language models. While industry setbacks and methodological critiques have highlighted gaps in evidence and challenges in scaling these technologies, emerging solutions rooted in co-design, rigorous evaluation, and implementation science offer promising pathways forward. This paper underscores the dual necessity of advancing the scientific foundations of digital mental health and increasing its real-world applicability through five themes. First, we discuss recent technological advances in digital phenotyping, virtual reality, and generative artificial intelligence. Progress in this latter area, specifically designed to create new outputs such as conversations and images, holds unique potential for the mental health field. Given the spread of smartphone apps, we then evaluate the evidence supporting their utility across various mental health contexts, including well-being, depression, anxiety, schizophrenia, eating disorders, and substance use disorders. This broad view of the field highlights the need for a new generation of more rigorous, placebo-controlled, and real-world studies. We subsequently explore engagement challenges that hamper all digital mental health tools, and propose solutions, including human support, digital navigators, just-in-time adaptive interventions, and personalized approaches. We then analyze implementation issues, emphasizing clinician engagement, service integration, and scalable delivery models. We finally consider the need to ensure that innovations work for all people and thus can bridge digital health disparities, reviewing the evidence on ta

Sustainable Consumption and Branding for Gen Z: How Brand Dimensions Influence Consumer Behavior and Adoption of Newly Launched Technological Products
hot.abstract: Generation Z is emerging as a powerful force in shaping global consumer behavior, particularly in the market of digital and technological products. This study examines how specific branding dimensions, such as online brand experience, engagement, image, trust, loyalty, awareness, behavioral intention, and brand knowledge, influence Gen Z’s purchase intention, emphasizing sustainable consumption. Sustainable consumption, in this context, refers to the preference for tech products that minimize the environmental impact through eco-friendly design, energy efficiency, and responsible sourcing. Using a quantitative approach, this cross-sectional research explores the effects of online brand experience, engagement, image, trust, loyalty, awareness, behavioral intention, and knowledge on purchasing newly launched technological products that align with sustainability. Data were collected from a Gen Z sample using a combination of convenience and systematic sampling, and multiple regression analysis identified the most significant predictors of purchase intention. The results indicate that online brand experience, brand image, brand trust, and brand loyalty play the most crucial roles, having a greater effects on Gen Z’s purchase intention, while brand awareness and knowledge also contribute. However, brand engagement and behavioral intention have weaker effects. These findings suggest that brands targeting Gen Z should prioritize building a strong, trustworthy, and engaging online presence while highlighting their sustainability efforts, and when Gen Z consumers have favorable digital interactions with a brand, perceive its image positively, trust it, and feel loyal to it, they are more likely to consider purchasing its sustainable offerings. This study enhances the understandi

hot.title: Leading in the Digital Age: The Role of Leadership in Organizational Digital Transformation
hot.abstract: In the modern digital age, organizations face unprecedented challenges and possibilities while managing the intricacies of digital transformation. Accelerated technological developments, changing customer preferences, heightened competition, and dynamic regulatory environments necessitate companies to synchronize their business goals with technological innovations. Leadership is crucial in steering businesses through changes, requiring a deep understanding of change processes and the capacity to adjust leadership accordingly. This research addresses the central question: How does leadership effectively promote organizational digital transformation? The study examines how leaders can effectively promote the adoption of advanced technologies and the promotion of innovation, by first exploring the nature of digital transformation within organizations and then analyzing the evolving dynamics of leadership in this context. An integrative review of the Web of Science (WoS) and Scopus databases was conducted, using the search terms: “Leadership” and “Digital Transformation”. The findings emphasize that effective leadership is crucial for managing the minutiae of digital transformation, integrating technology into organizational processes to facilitate learning, collaboration, and agility, enabling companies to adapt to market shifts, reduce uncertainty, and enhance decision-making for sustainable growth. By using the right tools and with the right frequency, leaders may develop team cohesion—even at a distance. Attentive digital-age leaders will know how to leverage the right mechanisms, and herein, we hope to give some indication of how that may be achieved, so that digital transformation increases rather than decreases team motivation levels.
hot.subfield: Organizational Behavior and Human Resource Management

hot.title: Building trust in sustainable brands: Revisiting perceived value, satisfaction, customer service, and brand image
hot.abstract: This study revisits the key variables that build brand trust in consumers, addressing a critical issue for building lasting relationships between brands and consumers. Through a conceptual model, we examine how perceived value, satisfaction, customer service, and brand image influence consumer trust. The research is based on a sample of 1280 Spanish consumers over the age of 18, who responded to a questionnaire designed with previously validated scales. The PLS-SEM technique was used to validate the hypotheses and the proposed model. The findings reveal that perceived value, satisfaction, customer service, and brand image have a positive and significant effect on consumer trust. In particular, it was found that customer service directly influences customer satisfaction, which in turn reinforces brand trust. Additionally, the brand's communication strategy shows a significant positive relationship with brand image. Finally, customer satisfaction is identified as a mediating variable in the relationship between customer service and trust, indicating that a positive experience with customer service is fundamental for consolidating brand trust. This study contributes to enhancing the understanding of the factors that promote brand trust and offers practical implications for the development of effective marketing and brand management strategies. These insights can be especially relevant for sustainable brands, as the identified factors—perceived value, satisfaction, customer service, and brand image—are also critical in fostering trust in brands that prioritize sustainability. Incorporating sustainable practices into these areas may further strengthen consumer trust and loyalty toward sustainable brands.

hot.title: Why human–AI relationships need socioaffective alignment
hot.abstract: Humans strive to design safe AI systems that align with our goals and remain under our control. However, as AI capabilities advance, we face a new challenge: the emergence of deeper, more persistent relationships between humans and AI systems. We explore how increasingly capable AI agents may generate the perception of deeper relationships with users, especially as AI becomes more personalised and agentic. This shift, from transactional interaction to ongoing sustained social engagement with AI, necessitates a new focus on socioaffective alignment—how an AI system behaves within the social and psychological ecosystem co-created with its user, where preferences and perceptions evolve through mutual influence. Addressing these dynamics involves resolving key intrapersonal dilemmas, including balancing immediate versus long-term well-being, protecting autonomy, and managing AI companionship alongside the desire to preserve human social bonds. By framing these challenges through a notion of basic psychological needs, we seek AI systems that support, rather than exploit, our fundamental nature as social and emotional beings.

hot.title: The moderating role of personalized recommendations in the trust–satisfaction–loyalty relationship: an empirical study of AI-driven e-commerce
hot.abstract: Abstract Purpose This study investigates the effects of trust, satisfaction, and loyalty on AI-driven e-commerce, with a particular focus on how personalized recommendations moderate these relationships. It aims to explore how personalized AI features reshape consumer perceptions and decision-making. Design/methodology/approach A quantitative research approach was used to collect data from a diverse group of e-commerce users who had interacted with AI-based recommendation systems. An online survey employing standardized scales for trust, satisfaction, loyalty, and personalization was administered, and data were analyzed using structural equation modeling (SEM) to test the hypotheses. Findings The study reveals that trust has a significant positive influence on both satisfaction and loyalty. Personalization further strengthens these relationships by moderating the trust–satisfaction–loyalty dynamic. Satisfaction partially mediates the relationship between trust and loyalty, with the model’s explanatory power improving by 5% when personalization is included as a moderator. These results highlight the pivotal role of personalized recommendations in shaping consumer trust and satisfaction in AI-driven e-commerce. Practical implications Businesses can use personalized recommendation systems to enhance trust and satisfaction, thereby fostering loyalty. For example, platforms like Amazon and Netflix have successfully employed personalized AI algorithms to boost customer retention and engagement. Transparency features, such as explaining why certain products are recommended, and cultural sensitivity in algorithm design can further enhance customer trust and acceptance. e-commerce organizations should also invest in data privacy measures and clear algorithms to maintain consumer

hot.title: The Typing Cure: Experiences with Large Language Model Chatbots for Mental Health Support
hot.venue: Proceedings of the ACM on Human-Computer Interaction
hot.abstract: People experiencing severe distress increasingly use Large Language Model (LLM) chatbots as mental health support tools. Discussions on social media have described how engagements were lifesaving for some, but evidence suggests that general-purpose LLM chatbots also have notable risks that could endanger the welfare of users if not designed responsibly. In this study, we investigate the lived experiences of people who have used LLM chatbots for mental health support. We build on interviews with 21 individuals from globally diverse backgrounds to analyze how users create unique support roles for their chatbots, fill in gaps in everyday care, and navigate associated cultural limitations when seeking support from chatbots. We ground our analysis in psychotherapy literature around effective support, and introduce the concept of therapeutic alignment, or aligning AI with therapeutic values for mental health contexts. Our study offers recommendations for how designers can approach the ethical and effective use of LLM chatbots and other AI mental health support tools in mental health care.

hot.title: AI-driven personalization: Unraveling consumer perceptions in social media engagement
A Glance on Changing Workplace Dynamics Post Covid-19 in India: A Review of Psychological Employee Withdrawal Behavior
hot.abstract: Advances in Consumer Research (Abbreviated as Adv. Consum. Res.) is a distinguished journal based in the United States and published by Sheridan Books. The journal is highly regarded in the academic community, particularly within the fields of Business, Management, and Accounting, with a specific focus on Marketing.

hot.title: Confronting and alleviating AI resistance in the workplace: An integrative review and a process framework
hot.abstract: This study involves an integrative literature review and a process framework explaining the mechanisms to confront and alleviate employee Artificial intelligence (AI) resistance in organizations. First, we conceptualize AI resistance as a three-dimensional concept embodied in employees' fears, inefficacies, and antipathies toward AI. We advance that experiencing mistrust, existential questioning, and technological reflection are key individual mechanisms to confronting AI resistance connected to organizational mechanisms to alleviate AI resistance through the continuous interaction and unfolding of anxiety and introspection. We also explain the alleviation of AI resistance as an organizational process consisting of AI accessibility, human-AI augmentation, and AI-technology legitimation, each of which maps into one of the dimensions in the employee-level confrontation mechanisms. Overall, our conceptual framework provides an overarching and granular understanding of AI resistance, how employees confront it, and how it can be alleviated in the workplace. • Develops a process framework explaining the mechanisms to confront and alleviate employee AI resistance. • AI resistance as a three-dimensional concept embodied in employees' fears, inefficacies, and antipathies toward AI. • Highlights mistrust, existential questioning, and technological reflection as key individual concerns • AI resistance is alleviated through AI accessibility, human-AI augmentation, and AI-technology legitimation.
hot.subfield: Organizational Behavior and Human Resource Management

hot.title: Gamification in education and training: A literature review
hot.abstract: Abstract Gamification, when properly implemented in education and training, can increase the engagement and motivation of learners and inspire them to change aspects of their behaviour to support learning. Although the use of gamification in the learning process might have a positive impact, its potential to strengthen education and training has not yet been confirmed. The descriptive literature review presented in this article synthesises studies and findings on the use of gamification in the education and training context. The authors used the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) model to select and analyse 46 publications from six bibliographic databases. They investigated the gamification theories, frameworks, models, elements and mechanics that can support learning. In addition, research was conducted to identify constraints, challenges and organisational impediments that may arise in gamified education and training programmes, to answer the question of how gamification can be implemented to achieve better learning outcomes. Findings show that further studies need to be conducted into this evolving learning approach. Overall, gamification is most likely to be effective when instructional design principles are used to ensure training content meets learners’ needs and expectations.

hot.title: AI and employee wellbeing in the workplace: An empirical study
hot.abstract: The integration of artificial intelligence (AI) in workplace settings significantly affects employees, particularly their wellbeing. Despite its growing relevance, the impact of AI on employee wellbeing remains underexplored. To address this gap, we conducted a survey and employed structural equation modeling to analyze data from Finnish and international companies headquartered in Finland (n = 207). We found that AI adoption does not directly impact employee wellbeing but indirectly influences it through work-related factors of task optimization and safety.
