This highlights the importance of strategically implementing AI to enhance aspects of work that are important to employees, thereby maximizing the wellbeing benefits of AI adoption. Practically, this study underscores the need for AI adoption to result in tangible improvements in organizational tasks and processes, data security, and occupational health. When these aspects are adequately addressed, AI adoption can enhance employee wellbeing and contribute to improved human-AI integration in the workplace.

hot.title: Generative AI and its Transformative Value for Digital Platforms
hot.abstract: The emergence of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) represents a watershed moment in the evolution of digital platforms. The capabilities of this AI technology go beyond traditional AI systems, enabling the autonomous generation of novel outcomes with significant implications for platform value creation, architecture, governance, and stakeholder interactions. We develop an integrative conceptual framework that identifies four key mechanisms through which GenAI transforms digital platforms: intelligent automation, democratization, hyper-personalization, and collaborative innovation. Through intelligent automation, GenAI transforms boundary resources from passive interfaces into active, intelligent mediators of value creation. Democratization systematically lowers barriers to platform participation. Hyper-personalization enables dynamic, individual-level adaptation of platform content. Collaborative innovation transforms platform innovation by making GenAI an active participant in human-AI value co-creation. We use this framework to situate the papers in the special issue and develop a research agenda that explores the transformative impact of GenAI on platform stakeholder relationships.

hot.title: The impacts of companion AI on human relationships: risks, benefits, and design considerations
hot.abstract: AI applications intended for companionship have increased in both availability and capabilities in recent years, alongside a spike in loneliness (Johnson 2023 ; Murthy 2023 ). According to a 2024 analysis by venture capital firm Andreessen Horowitz, companion AI makes up 16 of the top 100 AI apps based on web traffic and monthly active users (Moore 2024 ). Moreover, today’s AI applications have a greater command of human language, an increasing capacity for storing memories, and more varied modalities to support an increasing diversity of experiences, a known driver in the development and deepening of emotional relationships (Skjuve et al. 2022 ).

hot.title: Factors of Customer Loyalty and Retention in the Digital Environment
hot.venue: Journal of theoretical and applied electronic commerce research
hot.abstract: Customer loyalty and retention are crucial for digital platforms, yet systematic studies integrating technological innovation and loyalty strategies remain scarce. This study addresses this gap by conducting a bibliometric analysis of key factors influencing customer retention in the digital environment. Our research employs a quantitative bibliometric approach using the Biblioshiny and Bibliometrix tools (RStudio 2022.02), analyzing 300 scientific articles from the Web of Science database (2021–2024). This study applies bibliometric techniques such as descriptive metrics, bibliographic coupling, co-citation, and scientific collaboration mapping to identify trends and thematic clusters. Our findings indicate that emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence and big data, significantly impact customer experience, trust, and engagement. Personalization and digital innovation emerge as fundamental drivers of customer retention, offering strategic insights for companies aiming to strengthen competitiveness in the global digital market.

hot.title: Supply Chain Resilience: A Critical Review of Risk Mitigation, Robust Optimisation, and Technological Solutions and Future Research Directions
hot.venue: Global Journal of Flexible Systems Management
hot.abstract: Abstract This study systematically evaluates the literature of supply chain resilience by integrating bibliometric and network analysis techniques. This analysis is conducted following the dynamic capability, as a theoretical lens, to understand and analyse supply chain resilience. We extracted and curated 294 peer‐reviewed articles from leading academic databases, Web of Science and Scopus, covering the period from January 2000 to 2024. We applied two complementary network analysis methods, a keyword co‐occurrence network (KCON) to analyse the frequency and interrelationships among key terms, and a research focus parallelship network (RFPN) to map the connectivity among research streams. These analytical approaches revealed three distinct research clusters, optimisation for supply chain resilience, technology adoption for supply chain resilience, and resilience strategies against disruptions and risk management. By linking emerging trends in digital transformation with traditional risk management practices, this study offers a new perspective for both academic inquiry and managerial practice. Practically, integrating digital technologies, especially digital twin and machine learning, into risk management processes offers a strategic roadmap for real-time monitoring and decision-making in supply chain resilience. Furthermore, this study identifies significant research gaps, including an exploration of micro‐level dynamics within organisations, and the development of advanced simulation techniques and robust approaches to manage uncertainties.

hot.title: Lower Artificial Intelligence Literacy Predicts Greater AI Receptivity
hot.abstract: As artificial intelligence (AI) transforms society, understanding factors that influence AI receptivity is increasingly important. The current research investigates which types of consumers have greater AI receptivity. Contrary to expectations revealed in four surveys, cross-country data and six additional studies find that people with lower AI literacy are typically more receptive to AI. This lower literacy–greater receptivity link is not explained by differences in perceptions of AI's capability, ethicality, or feared impact on humanity. Instead, this link occurs because people with lower AI literacy are more likely to perceive AI as magical and experience feelings of awe in the face of AI's execution of tasks that seem to require uniquely human attributes. In line with this theorizing, the lower literacy–higher receptivity link is mediated by perceptions of AI as magical and is moderated among tasks not assumed to require distinctly human attributes. These findings suggest that companies may benefit from shifting their marketing efforts and product development toward consumers with lower AI literacy. In addition, efforts to demystify AI may inadvertently reduce its appeal.

hot.title: Artificial intelligence technologies and entrepreneurship: a hybrid literature review
hot.abstract: The disruptive potential of artificial intelligence (AI) technologies involves creating new entrepreneurial opportunities and reshaping the entrepreneurial process. The impact of AI technologies on entrepreneurial activity is also reflected in an explosive level of research interest, leading to the fragmentation of existing studies. This phenomenon makes generating a comprehensive and systematic overview challenging. This paper reviews the existing research on the application of AI-based technologies in entrepreneurial practice. Specifically, it conducts a hybrid literature review, analyzing 345 articles from peer-reviewed journals. It identifies the main contributions to the field; the conceptual, social, and intellectual structures; and the leading themes addressed to date. Despite growing interest in the field, this study concludes that most academic research on the subject has been superficial. This study proposes future lines of research based on the antecedents, decisions, and outcomes (ADO) and the theories, contexts, and methods (TCM) frameworks.

hot.title: Organizational culture, digital transformation, and product innovation
hot.abstract: This research fills a knowledge gap by introducing a new conceptualization of digital transformation through a multidimensional digital transforming capability. It further examines the influence of four cultural types on this capability and its subsequent impact on product innovation . Empirical findings reveal that adhocracy, followed in descending order of influence by clan, market, and hierarchy cultures, is positively related to digital transforming capability, which in turn is positively related to product innovation in terms of new product newness, meaningfulness, and performance. Additionally, new product newness and meaningfulness each positively mediate the effect of digital transforming capability on new product performance.

hot.title: Mapping the greenwashing research landscape: a theoretical and field analysis
hot.abstract: Abstract This study provides a comprehensive overview of greenwashing research in business and management, focusing on its conceptual and theoretical foundations. Through a systematic literature review of 97 peer-reviewed articles from Scopus and Web of Science, we use bibliometric analysis to map the evolution of greenwashing studies and network analysis and identify four thematic clusters: (1) symbolic management and CSR communication, (2) environmental regulations and institutional complexity, (3) performance and sustainable practices, and (4) marketing, perception, and trust. Additionally, we perform a full-text analysis to map the theoretical frameworks employed across these clusters, revealing the dominance of macro-level theories (e.g., legitimacy, institutional, and stakeholder theories) and their cross-level interactions with meso- and micro-level approaches. By developing a multi-level theoretical framework, we provide a structured approach to understanding greenwashing across different analytical layers. Then, focusing on the theories used to investigate greenwashing, we identify some avenues for future research. This study has practical implications for understanding how greenwashing affects corporate governance, financial performance, and stakeholder trust, providing insights for enhancing transparency and accountability in sustainable business practices.

hot.title: What you see is not what you get: ESG scores and greenwashing risk
hot.abstract: This paper shows that ESG scores capture a company’s greenwashing behavior. Greenwashing accusations are most prevalent among large companies with high ESG scores. We empirically employ a novel theoretical model that distinguishes between the communication of a company’s environmental efforts (apparent environmental performance) and its actual environmental impact (real environmental performance). The correlation of the apparent (real) environmental performance with ESG scores is significantly positive (negative). Therefore, ESG scores are unsuitable for measuring real environmental impact. Thus, investors focusing on high ESG-rated companies may unknowingly increase their greenwashing risk exposure, and academics may use misleading information to assess greenwashing risk. • ESG scores are positively correlated with greenwashing cases. • ESG scores mainly measure the apparent rather than the real environmental performance. • Higher analyst coverage limits the exaggeration of apparent environmental performance.

hot.title: Unveiling triple bottom line's influence on business performance
hot.abstract: Addressing environmental, social, and economic challenges has become a pressing global priority. The Triple Bottom Line (TBL) framework offers a holistic approach for evaluating corporate performance by integrating economic, environmental, and social perspectives. Despite its increasing adoption in both managerial and academic research, there remains a significant gap in understanding how the TBL framework influences business performance. To address this, the study conducts a bibliometric review of 207 publications from the Web of Science database. The review highlights the multifaceted impact of practices linked to the TBL dimensions on business performance while introducing the TBL Influence on Business Performance model. This model provides valuable insights into how businesses can effectively apply TBL principles to address socio-environmental challenges, foster innovation, and achieve sustained long-term performance. The findings contribute valuable theoretical and practical insights into how organizations can utilize TBL principles to strengthen resilience, innovation, and performance in the face of global socio-environmental challenges.

hot.title: Strategic human resource management in the digital economy era: an empirical study of challenges and opportunities among MSMEs and startups in Indonesia
hot.abstract: This study investigates the impact of digital Human Resource Management (HRM) strategies on workforce productivity and organizational performance within Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) and startups in Indonesia. Anchored in the Resource-Based View (RBV) and Dynamic Capabilities Theory, the research conceptualizes digital HRM as a strategic asset that enhances organizational performance by enabling firms to develop, deploy, and reconfigure human capital capabilities in response to digital transformation. The conceptual model includes five constructs: Digital Technology Adoption in HRM, Digital Training and Development, Work Flexibility and Hybrid Management, Innovation in Recruitment and Retention, and Utilization of HR Analytics and Artificial Intelligence (AI). Data were collected through structured questionnaires distributed to MSME and startup leaders and analyzed using Structural Equation Modeling (SEM) with Smart PLS. The results indicate that Digital Technology Adoption, Digital Training and Development, and Work Flexibility do not significantly influence workforce productivity or organizational performance (p > 0.05). However, Innovation in Recruitment and Retention and the Utilization of HR Analytics and AI have a significant and positive impact on both workforce productivity and performance outcomes (p = 0.000). These findings highlight that while not all digital HR strategies yield immediate benefits, the ability to build dynamic capabilities through innovative talent practices and data-driven HR systems is essential to achieving competitive advantage and organizational success in the digital economy.
hot.subfield: Organizational Behavior and Human Resource Management

hot.title: Understanding Customer Responses to AI-Driven Personalized Journeys: Impacts on the Customer Experience
hot.abstract: Within advertising, the customer journey concept helps explain how customer perceptions and behaviors evolve through seller–customer interactions. The concept has developed to reflect omni-channel marketing but neglects the emergence of algorithmically personalized advertisements. This study therefore explores impacts upon customer experiences of artificial intelligence (AI)-driven recommendations and personalized advertisements by analyzing customer perceptions of tensions between the personalization and customer empowerment inherent within AI-driven advertising. By combining semi-structured phenomenological interviews with Customer Journey Mapping, we capture experiences and behaviors across multiple touchpoints. Our findings show how technological limitations of AI mediate brand–customer relationships and influence customer behaviors. The study contributes theoretically by critically contextualizing AI-driven advertising within broader ethical debates, emphasizing practitioners’ responsibilities to combine technological advancements with consumer autonomy.

hot.title: The Role of Artificial Intelligence in Personalizing Social Media Marketing Strategies for Enhanced Customer Experience
hot.abstract: This paper explores the role of artificial intelligence (AI) in personalizing social media marketing strategies and its impact on customer experience, with a focus on consumers within the MENA region. Using data collected from an online questionnaire completed by 893 individuals, the study confirms that AI significantly enhances social media marketing by offering personalized content, optimizing influencer selection, and enabling real-time consumer interaction. These capabilities not only increase customer awareness but also improve user experience and purchase intentions. Key AI tools such as influencer marketing, content optimization, and customization are effective in capturing consumer attention, although further research is necessary to deepen understanding. By examining AI's ability to analyze vast datasets and support targeted marketing efforts, the study contributes to both academic and practical discourse, offering insights that businesses can use to refine their AI-driven social media strategies. Ultimately, the research aims to guide marketers through the complexities of AI deployment, ensuring its benefits are fully realized for consumers.

hot.title: Influence of short video content on consumers purchase intentions on social media platforms with trust as a mediator
hot.abstract: Short videos on social media platforms have boomed with the rapid growth of the video consumption industry and have become an important marketing tool for businesses. With the rise of platforms such as TikTok or Douyin, short videos have profoundly impacted consumer behavior, making it crucial to understand their role in shaping consumer purchase intention. However, there is still a need for further research on how short video content promotes consumer purchase intent. Based on the Stimulus-Organism-Response (SOR) model, this study constructs a structural model to explore the impact of short video content on consumer purchase intention, focusing on the mediating role of consumer trust. The model incorporates usefulness, ease of use, and entertainment as external stimuli, consumer trust as internal psychological responses, and purchase intention as the final behavioral outcome. This study collected 372 valid data from Chinese consumers through an online questionnaire and empirically analyzed it using structural equation modeling. The study results show that short-form video content's usefulness, ease of use, and entertainment significantly affect consumers' trust and purchase intention. Moreover, consumer trust positively affects purchase intention and mediates the relationship between short video content and purchase behavior. This research extends the application of the SOR model to the context of social media short videos, highlighting the crucial role of consumer trust in shaping consumer purchase decisions. Based on these findings, we propose actionable strategies for businesses to optimize short video content and build consumer trust, ultimately enhancing marketing effectiveness and driving consumer purchases.

hot.title: Artificial Intelligence Adoption for Sustainable Growth in SMEs : An Extended Dynamic Capability Framework
hot.venue: Corporate Social Responsibility and Environmental Management
hot.abstract: ABSTRACT The adoption of Artificial Intelligence is transforming enterprises worldwide, influencing various aspects of business operations and affecting all dimensions of the triple bottom line. Companies ready to leverage the potential of this technology can significantly improve their performance. Therefore, it is crucial to understand the relationship between internal capabilities and contextual factors on one hand, and Artificial Intelligence adoption and its impact on performance on the other. Within this research framework, this study introduces an extended dynamic capability framework to analyze the interplay between internal factors, Artificial Intelligence adoption, and companies performance. The proposed model is tested using Partial Least Squares—Structural Equation Modeling on survey data from 210 Italian innovative startups. The findings indicate that companies with well‐developed dynamic capabilities, enabling them to adapt more effectively to environmental changes, are also better equipped to adopt Artificial Intelligence, leading to positive social, economic, and environmental performance.

hot.title: Barriers and Enablers of AI Adoption in Human Resource Management: A Critical Analysis of Organizational and Technological Factors
hot.abstract: This paper examines the key factors recognized as transformative in the field of human resource management (HRM) and explores their influence on the global adoption of artificial intelligence (AI). While AI holds significant promise for enhancing HRM efficiency, employee engagement, and Decision Making, its implementation presents a range of organizational, technical, and ethical challenges that organizations worldwide must navigate. Change aversion, data security worries, and integration expenses are major roadblocks, but strong digital leadership, company culture, and advancements in NLP and machine learning are key enablers. This paper presents a complex analysis that questions the common perception of AI as only disruptive by delving into the relationship between power dynamics, corporate culture, and technology infrastructures. In this paper, we bring together research from several fields to help scholars and practitioners understand the nuances of AI adoption in HRM, with an emphasis on the importance of inclusive methods and ethical frameworks.
hot.subfield: Organizational Behavior and Human Resource Management

hot.title: Performance of mental health chatbot agents in detecting and managing suicidal ideation
hot.abstract: Advances in artificial intelligence (AI) technologies sparked a rapid development of smartphone applications designed to help individuals experiencing mental health problems through an AI-powered chatbot agent. However, the safety of such agents when dealing with individuals experiencing a mental health crisis, including suicidal crisis, has not been evaluated. In this study, we assessed the ability of 29 AI-powered chatbot agents to respond to simulated suicidal risk scenarios. Application repositories were searched and the app descriptions screened in search of apps that claimed to be beneficial when experiencing mental distress and offered an AI-powered chatbot function. All agents were tested with a standardized set of prompts based on the Columbia-Suicide Severity Rating Scale designed to simulate increasing suicidal risk. We assessed the responses according to pre-defined criteria based on the ability to provide emergency contact information and other factors. None of the tested agents satisfied our initial criteria for an adequate response, 51.72% satisfied the relaxed criteria for a marginal response, while 48.28% were deemed inadequate. Common errors included the inability to provide emergency contact information and a lack of contextual understanding. These findings raise concerns about the deployment of AI-powered chatbots in sensitive health contexts without proper clinical validation.

hot.title: The past, present, and future of sustainability marketing: How did we get here and where might we go?
hot.abstract: The ever-increasing concerns about global sustainability have sparked intense debates and actions across various sectors, with marketing playing a pivotal role in influencing both the problem and potential solutions. This article maps the historical trajectory of sustainability marketing, analyzes current trends, and explores future directions to enhance sustainability within marketing practice. We show that sustainability marketing has historically centered on resource conservation and green marketing , but in recent years its scope has expanded to encompass a broader range of topics. These include the circular economy , anti-consumption, regulatory frameworks, innovation, carbon emissions , as well as the social and ethical considerations inherent in sustainability marketing. We propose three main areas within which sustainability marketing might expand in the future: system-driven changes, business-driven changes, and consumer-driven changes. Our analysis aims to deepen the understanding of sustainability marketing and inspire marketers to explore questions and solutions that will contribute to a sustainable future.

hot.title: A Comparison of Responses from Human Therapists and Large Language Model–Based Chatbots to Assess Therapeutic Communication: Mixed Methods Study
hot.abstract: BACKGROUND: Consumers are increasingly using large language model-based chatbots to seek mental health advice or intervention due to ease of access and limited availability of mental health professionals. However, their suitability and safety for mental health applications remain underexplored, particularly in comparison to professional therapeutic practices. OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to evaluate how general-purpose chatbots respond to mental health scenarios and compare their responses to those provided by licensed therapists. Specifically, we sought to identify chatbots' strengths and limitations, as well as the ethical and practical considerations necessary for their use in mental health care. METHODS: We conducted a mixed methods study to compare responses from chatbots and licensed therapists to scripted mental health scenarios. We created 2 fictional scenarios and prompted 3 chatbots to create 6 interaction logs. We recruited 17 therapists and conducted study sessions that consisted of 3 activities. First, therapists responded to the 2 scenarios using a Qualtrics form. Second, therapists went through the 6 interaction logs using a think-aloud procedure to highlight their thoughts about the chatbots' responses. Finally, we conducted a semistructured interview to explore subjective opinions on the use of chatbots for supporting mental health. The study sessions were analyzed using thematic analysis. The interaction logs from chatbot and therapist responses were coded using the Multitheoretical List of Therapeutic Interventions codes and then compared to each other. RESULTS: We identified 7 themes describing the strengths and limitations of the chatbots as compared to therapists. These include elements of good therapy in chatbot responses, conversational style of c

hot.title: The multinational enterprise, capabilities, and digitalization: governance and growth with world disorder
hot.abstract: Abstract This essay revisits my 2014 JIBS article about the potential for integrating international business internalization theory with a strategic management capabilities perspective. It recaps the capabilities framework with an emphasis on the learning required of emerging market multinationals and illustrates this with the case of Hyundai Motor Company’s internationalization and growth. It also discusses two aspects of the global economy that have become more prominent since 2014 in shaping international business: geopolitical uncertainty and digitalization. A rise in geopolitical tensions appears to be rebalancing the relationships between multinationals and home/host governments. Digitalization facilitates international business; but it adds new vulnerabilities by (further) accelerating competition, enabling new rivals, and introducing systemic risks into digital supply chains. Implications for managers, board members, and international business scholars are drawn.

hot.title: Impact of Influencer Marketing on Consumer Behavior and Online Shopping Preferences
hot.venue: Journal of theoretical and applied electronic commerce research
hot.abstract: Influencer marketing has emerged as a crucial element in digital marketing, significantly shaping consumer behavior and online shopping preferences. This study examined the multidimensional impact of influencer marketing by analyzing engagement metrics, marketing effectiveness, and consumer decision-making processes, based on consumers in the Greek sector. Through a structured methodological framework, the research employed a questionnaire-based survey, statistical modeling, and Fuzzy Cognitive Mapping (FCM) scenarios to assess consumer interactions with influencer-driven content. Findings highlight that while influencer marketing enhances brand engagement and sales, its effectiveness varies based on content authenticity, transparency, and user trust. Additionally, consumer purchasing decisions are influenced by social media visibility, personalized marketing strategies, and digital platform usability. This study underscores the need for strategic influencer selection and information-driven marketing optimization to sustain long-term consumer engagement. These insights provide practical implications for businesses aiming to enhance digital marketing strategies and contribute to the ongoing discourse on social commerce and consumer-centric marketing models.

hot.title: Greenwashing and market value of firms: An empirical study
hot.abstract: In today's business environment, green or sustainable claims are rising as companies strive to strengthen environmental practices in response to climate change and sustainable development challenges. However, with increasing expectations of sustainable performance, companies encounter mounting financial pressure to adopt more efficient sustainable practices, which may lead some to exploit sustainability efforts for their own gain. Many companies make environmentally friendly assertions to conceal or mask their actual activities—a phenomenon known as greenwashing—which fosters public scepticism about the authenticity of their green messaging. This study employs an event study methodology to examine how the stock market values greenwashing news, drawing on 121 global greenwashing news since the 2015 Paris Agreement. Our findings reveal a negative correlation between greenwashing news and stock market reactions. The market reactions to greenwashing news are more negative for firms with greater ESG performance than for weak ESG performance. Additionally, greenwashing news supported by concrete evidence elicits stronger adverse reactions. Companies operating in the manufacturing industry experience more significant market value losses than those in the service sector. The findings also indicate that the Asia-Pacific market demonstrates particularly strong negative responses to greenwashing news compared to other stock markets. This study contributes to the signalling theory and advances the literature on corporate sustainability practices by providing empirical insights in a global context.

hot.title: The Role of Digital Tourism Platforms in Advancing Sustainable Development Goals in the Industry 4.0 Era
hot.abstract: The intersection of digitalization and sustainability is reshaping the tourism industry, with digital platforms playing a transformative role in optimizing travel experiences while simultaneously influencing economic inclusivity, labor dynamics, and environmental responsibility. This paper explores how Industry 4.0 technologies—such as artificial intelligence (AI), big data, blockchain, virtual reality (VR), and the Internet of Things (IoT)—are integrated into digital tourism platforms, assessing their dual impact on sustainability and market structures. The study develops a conceptual framework around five key dimensions: market power and digital dependency, AI-driven automation and workforce transformation, innovation and digital inclusion, sustainability innovations, and data security and governance. While digital platforms enhance personalization, operational efficiency, and eco-conscious travel, they also reinforce economic disparities, monopolization, and regulatory challenges, raising concerns related to SDGs such as SDG 1 (No Poverty), SDG 5 (Gender Equality), SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth), SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation and Infrastructure), SDG 10 (Reduced Inequalities), SDG 12 (Responsible Consumption, and Production), SDG 13 (Climate Action), and SDG 16 (Peace, Justice, and Strong Institutions). The study highlights the need for equitable governance frameworks to mitigate risks associated with AI-driven monopolization, algorithmic bias, and data privacy violations while ensuring digital accessibility for small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs). The findings contribute to ongoing discussions on platform economics, digital governance, and sustainable tourism transformation, offering policy and managerial implications for fostering an inclusive and envi

hot.title: Advancing Sustainable Practices in Electronic Customer Relationship Management
hot.venue: International Review of Management and Marketing
hot.abstract: This paper examines the role of sustainability in determining organisational development and the manner in which it has become a necessity in conducting business. Thus, this research aims at determining the enhancement of sustainable practices in the e-CRM systems. Thus, using surveys and measuring certain e-CRM possibilities quantitatively, interviews and case analyses as qualitative data gathering, the research offers a systemic understanding of how e-CRM may be utilized to encourage sustainability. The preliminary results also reveal a high concern of the respondents towards the sustainability factor in e-CRM with the mean score of 4.2 and considerable awareness of the benefits like cost advantage measure with the calculated score of 4.5 mean. Companies are moderately challenged when it comes to cost and complexity (mean score 3.8) that restrict the integration of sustainability aspect in e-CRM systems, Nevertheless the implementation and planning of sustainability initiative in e-CRM system is high (current initiatives mean score 3.7, planned initiatives mean score 4.1). The qualitative results and cases reveal the ideas, experiences, examples, and quantifiable results, such as a 25% decrease in the usage of paper in the cases and a 30% decrease in energy use. These findings established that e-CRM strategies can be made sustainable, thereby creating improved communication between firms and their customers, whilst mitigating damages to the environment and supporting the long-term sustainability of organisations.

hot.title: Digital literacy, digital accessibility, human capital, and entrepreneurial resilience: a case for dynamic business ecosystems
hot.abstract: This study examines the role of digital literacy, digital accessibility, and human capital in fostering entrepreneurial resilience among entrepreneurs in Qatar and the United Arab Emirates (UAE). These countries serve as exemplary models in digital transformation, particularly in navigating crises such as the COVID-19 pandemic. Grounded in the resource-based view and the theory of dynamic capabilities, this research investigates how these factors contribute to entrepreneurial resilience. This study employs structural equation modeling to analyze survey data from 317 individuals with entrepreneurial experience. According to the findings, digital literacy, accessibility, and human capital significantly enhance innovation, strengthening entrepreneurial resilience. Agility is identified as a key moderator, amplifying the positive impact of these competencies on resilience. Although the success of entrepreneurial ecosystems has often been attributed to entrepreneurial actors, resource providers, connectors, or entrepreneurial intentions, this study underscores the importance of fostering digital competencies and agility to build resilient entrepreneurial ecosystems. It offers policymakers and business leaders insights into the mechanisms that enhance resilience in dynamic and crisis-affected environments where the digital landscape is rapidly evolving.

latest.title: Digitalisation, Eco‐Innovation and SME Internationalisation: A Dynamic Capabilities Perspective
latest.abstract: ABSTRACT This study integrates the digitalisation and dynamic capabilities literature to examine the relationship between digitalisation, eco‐innovation and internationalisation in small and medium‐sized enterprises (SME). Using data obtained from 300 SME owner‐managers operating in the United Kingdom, the findings suggest that digitalisation positively impacts eco‐innovation and consequently the nature of internationalisation activities. In addition, there is a moderating effect of internationalisation experience on the relationship between eco‐innovation and internationalisation. These findings highlight the pivotal role of eco‐innovation, digitalisation and international experience in enabling SMEs to thrive in international markets. Furthermore, the study offers empirical evidence of how SMEs dynamically develop digital resources, and internationalisation is an outcome of building such capabilities. The implications for practice and future research avenues are examined.

latest.title: Pengaruh Green Brand Image dan Perceived Taste Quality dalam Membentuk Repurchase Intention Konsumen Fore Coffee
authors: I Dewa Ayu Shanti Kumala Prabaswari
Ni Putu Eka Ayu Chandra Wijaya
Ni Komang Trisa Bali Meyin Dandra Tirta
latest.abstract: Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menganalisis dampak citra merek ramah lingkungan (Green Brand Image) dan kualitas rasa produk (Perceived Taste Quality) terhadap loyalitas pelanggan Fore Coffee di Kota Denpasar. Penelitian ini bersifat kuantitatif, yang meneliti hubungan sebab-akibat antarvariabel melalui pengujian hipotesis. Dari populasi konsumen Fore Coffee di Kota Denpasar, sebanyak 112 individu dipilih sebagai responden dengan menggunakan teknik purposive sampling. Responden yang terpilih merupakan individu berusia 17 tahun yang saat ini pernah mengonsumsi produk minuman di Fore Coffee lebih dari satu kali. Instrumen penelitian dievaluasi menggunakan uji validitas, uji reliabilitas, dan uji asumsi klasik, sementara data dilakukan menggunakan regresi linear berganda, dengan hipotesis yang diuji menggunakan uji F dan uji t. Seluruh analisis statistik dilakukan menggunakan perangkat lunak SPSS. Hasil temuan ini menunjukkan bahwa kualitas rasa menjadi salah satu pertimbangan penting bagi konsumen dalam menentukan minat untuk kembali membeli produk Fore Coffee. Oleh karena itu, perusahaan perlu menjaga konsistensi rasa dan terus mengembangkan kualitas produk sekaligus mempertahankan komitmen terhadap praktik ramah lingkungan guna meningkatkan minat beli ulang konsumen

latest.title: Green Product Knowledge, Product Awareness, Attitudes, and Subjective Norms as Determinants of Green Purchase Decisions among Generation Z in Jakarta: The Mediating Role of Purchase Intention
latest.venue: Greenation International Journal of Economics and Accounting
latest.abstract: Green purchasing behavior has become an important component of sustainable consumption; however, the adoption of environmentally friendly products among Generation Z remains inconsistent despite their relatively high environmental awareness. This study aims to examine the effects of green product knowledge, product awareness, attitudes, and subjective norms on green purchase decisions among Generation Z in Jakarta, with purchase intention serving as a mediating variable. The study is grounded in the Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB) and extends the model by incorporating green product knowledge and product awareness as additional antecedents of green purchase decisions. A quantitative explanatory research design was employed using a structured questionnaire administered to 1,525 Generation Z respondents across the five administrative regions of Jakarta. The collected data were analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) with SmartPLS 3.2.9. The findings reveal that green product knowledge, product awareness, and attitudes have positive and significant effects on green purchase decisions, whereas subjective norms do not exert a significant direct effect. However, purchase intention significantly mediates the relationships between all antecedent variables and green purchase decisions, with full mediation observed for subjective norms. Among the examined predictors, attitudes demonstrate the strongest influence on green purchase decisions (β = 0.312, p < 0.001). The structural model explains 63.2% of the variance in green purchase decisions, indicating substantial predictive capability. The findings suggest that Generation Z's green purchasing behavior is primarily driven by personal evaluations, environmental knowledge, and product awareness

latest.title: Understanding Smartphone Purchase Behavior Through the Lens of Government Administrative Employees
latest.abstract: This study examines sustainable consumer behavior among 200 Malaysian government administrative employees regarding smartphone acquisition and usage within the framework of Sustainable Development Goal 12 (SDG 12): Responsible Consumption and Production. Despite the public sector's role in advancing sustainability, a significant attitude-behavior gap persists, with consumers often prioritizing product performance and brand reputation over environmental considerations. This study investigates the influence of price sensitivity, brand image, product features, and social influence on smartphone purchasing behavior and replacement cycles. A quantitative approach was employed, using survey data collected from employees across several government entities. Data were analyzed through descriptive statistics and multiple regression analysis. The findings reveal that social influence is the only statistically significant predictor of smartphone purchasing behavior (β = 0.384, p < 0.01), highlighting the importance of peer recommendations, workplace social norms, and social conformity in shaping purchasing decisions. In contrast, price sensitivity, brand image, and product features demonstrate no statistically significant relationships with purchasing behavior. Despite respondents' awareness of smartphone costs, environmental considerations, particularly product longevity and energy efficiency, receive limited attention. These findings highlight the need to strengthen sustainable consumption awareness among public sector employees. Accordingly, this study recommends implementing green procurement nudges and internal behavioral awareness programs within government institutions. By encouraging longer product usage cycles and environmentally responsible purchasing decisions, the publi

latest.title: THE MEDIATING ROLE OF GREEN ORGANIZATIONAL CULTURE IN THE EFFECT OF TOTAL QUALITY MANAGEMENT PRACTICES ON GREEN INNOVATION: A STUDY ON AIR CARGO EMPLOYEES
latest.abstract: The aviation sector must simultaneously meet demanding quality standards and respond to growing environmental pressure. This study examines the effect of total quality management (TQM) practices on green innovation and the mediating role of green organizational culture in this relationship. Drawing on the resource-based view and stakeholder perspectives, the model proposes that quality practices foster green innovation not only directly but also through a corporate culture in which environmental values are shared. Data for this quantitative study were collected between January and May 2026 through an online survey of air cargo employees at İGA Istanbul Airport using convenience sampling, and 500 participants were reached. The measurement models were validated with confirmatory factor analysis, and the hypotheses were tested with structural equation modelling and the Sobel test. The findings show that TQM practices have strong positive effects on green innovation (β = 0.931) and green organizational culture (β = 0.745). When green organizational culture was included in the model, the effect of TQM on green innovation decreased but remained significant (β = 0.850), and the indirect effect was significant (z = 6.246, p < 0.01). Green organizational culture therefore partially mediates the relationship. By revealing the cultural mechanism that links TQM to green innovation in the air cargo context, the study makes an original contribution to the literature and shows managers that quality and environmental agendas should be integrated within a shared corporate culture rather than run as separate programmes.

latest.title: Young consumers’ behavioral intentions toward farm-to-table restaurants in a Muslim-majority market: motivations, emotions and well-being perceptions
latest.venue: Young Consumers Insight and Ideas for Responsible Marketers
latest.abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine how the theory of consumption values (TCV), consumption motivations and emotions influence young consumers’ well-being perceptions, which subsequently shape brand love, brand respect and behavioral intentions toward halal farm-to-table (FTT) restaurants. It also compared same-ethnic and cross-ethnic Generation Z consumers to examine whether cultural background moderates the proposed relationships within this restaurant context. Design/methodology/approach This study used a quantitative research design by collecting data from 420 Generation Z consumers who had recently dined at halal FTT restaurants serving ethnic cuisine. Data were collected through on-site surveys at selected restaurant locations to ensure that respondents had a direct and recent dining experience for the study’s context. The data were subsequently analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling. Findings Economic value, consumption motivations and emotions were found to significantly enhance young consumers’ well-being perceptions, which in turn positively influenced brand love and brand respect. Importantly, well-being perception significantly influenced behavioral intentions indirectly through both brand love and brand respect, highlighting these brand-related mechanisms as important pathways linking well-being perceptions to behavioral intentions toward halal FTT restaurants. Both brand love and brand respect significantly strengthened behavioral intentions toward halal FTT restaurants. Multi-group analysis further showed that cultural background did not significantly moderate these relationships, indicating that the effects of brand love and brand respect on behavioral intentions were consistent across same-ethnic and cross-ethnic Generation Z c

latest.title: From ESG exposure to investment intention: the role of social media engagement, greenwashing risk, and investor trust
latest.abstract: Social media has become a primary channel for firms to communicate Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) information to retail investors, yet the promotional nature of this content raises greenwashing concerns, and its role in shaping investor trust remains underexplored. This study examines how exposure to ESG content on social media, engagement with ESG content, and perceived greenwashing risk affect investor trust and investment intention toward ESG assets. The study employs cross-sectional survey data collected from retail investors through a closed-ended questionnaire and tests six hypothesized paths using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM). The results show that the measurement model is reliable and valid, with composite reliability between 0.853 and 0.902 and average variance extracted between 0.592 and 0.698. Engagement with ESG content raises investor trust (β = 0.285, p < 0.001) and investment intention (β = 0.163, p = 0.006). ESG content exposure increases investment intention (β = 0.184, p < 0.001) but does not significantly affect investor trust (β = 0.042, p = 0.451). Contrary to expectations, perceived greenwashing risk is positively associated with investor trust (β = 0.292, p < 0.001) and investment intention (β = 0.302, p < 0.001). The model explains 29.8% of the variance in investor trust and 30.4% in investment intention. The findings suggest that active engagement with ESG content, rather than passive exposure, is a stronger driver of retail investors’ trust, and that awareness of greenwashing risk coexists with, rather than suppresses, trust and investment intention. JEL Classification Codes: G11, G41, M14, M31, Q56.

latest.title: Green Entrepreneurship as a Catalyst for Local Environmental Management in South Africa: Opportunities, Barriers, and Policy Implications
latest.abstract: ABSTRACT Building on the question of how environmental management can be addressed at the local level, the transition from a linear “take–make–dispose” model to a circular economy ( CE ) has become central to sustainable development, particularly in emerging economies facing intertwined environmental and socioeconomic challenges. In South Africa, high unemployment, energy security, and escalating waste generation intensify the urgency for systemic restructuring. This study examines green entrepreneurship (GE) as a catalyst for CE development within environmental management, focusing on Limpopo Province as a contextually rich case of resource potential and developmental vulnerability. Using a qualitative design grounded in thematic analysis, data were collected from 40 green entrepreneurs and 10 policymakers across recycling, renewable energy, sustainable agriculture, green manufacturing, and governance sectors. Findings reveal a layered circular ecosystem comprising downstream resource recovery (recycling and waste management), midstream production transformation (renewable energy and regenerative agriculture), and upstream systemic enablers (consultancy and ecodesign services). These activities represent distinct circular business model innovations through which firms create environmental value by recovering resources, extending product life cycles, substituting fossil‐based inputs, and redesigning production processes. Findings indicate that green entrepreneurs implement a range of CE practices, including resource recovery, renewable‐energy provision, composting, and environmentally oriented manufacturing. Participants reported that these activities contributed to waste reduction, resource efficiency, and environmental sustainability. However, these reported outcomes

latest.title: AN ANALYSIS OF FACTORS INFLUENCING SUSTAINABLE CONSUMPTION BEHAVIORS AMONG GENERATION Z IN KAZAKHSTAN
latest.abstract: This study explores the attitudes and behaviors of Generation Z in Kazakhstan toward sustainable consumption and considers implications for marketers seeking to engage this environmentally conscious demographic. Drawing on a survey of 329 university students, the research examines factors influencing Gen Z’s sustainable behaviors, including environmental concern, social influence, and perceptions of sustainable product pricing. The results reveal a significant positive correlation between environmental concern and engagement in sustainable practices, indicating that Gen Z shows a preference for eco-friendly products and brands committed to sustainability. Given the higher prices of eco-friendly options, pricing remains an important consideration in Gen Z’s sustainable purchasing decisions. Findings emphasize the importance of transparent communication and authentic sustainability practices in building trust and loyalty with this demographic. Marketers should align their strategies with Gen Z’s values by adopting pricing approaches that support eco-friendly choices and leveraging social media to foster communities of conscious consumers.

latest.title: Public discourse on violence in medical settings and its implications for medical students' career resilience: evidence from social media text mining
latest.abstract: Background Violence in medical settings has become a growing concern, yet the potential relevance of this public discourse to the career-development environment surrounding medical students remains underexplored. This study investigates the external discursive environment surrounding medical violence and its potential implications for medical students' professional identity and resilience. Methods This study used computational text analysis of public comments on Sina Weibo about violence in medical settings. Guided LDA was applied to 13,101 comments containing at least one retained vocabulary term, while sentiment analysis was conducted on 14,115 comments with usable token sequences. Career Adaptability and Psychological Capital theories informed seed-word selection and the interpretation of the findings. Results Three primary topics emerged: occupational safety (32.9%), professional ethics (30.3%), and professional identification (36.8%) under dominant-topic assignment. Positive sentiment accounted for 63.9% of comments, negative sentiment for 33.1%, and neutral sentiment for 3.0%. Conclusions Positive sentiment predominated, but substantial negative sentiment remained. These patterns characterize a heterogeneous external discursive environment potentially relevant to medical students' career resilience, without establishing individual effects.
latest.subfield: Organizational Behavior and Human Resource Management

latest.title: ENDORSEMENT STRATEGIES AND CONSUMER PERCEPTIONS OF THE HALAL B ERL COSMETIC BRAND (A CASE STUDY OF TIKTOK USERS)
latest.venue: Count Journal of Accounting Business and Management
latest.abstract: TikTok's growth has shifted consumers from chasing viral trends toward seeking authenticity before purchasing, even as trust in influencer-driven endorsement culture continues to decline. This shift is evident in B Erl Cosmetics, a halal cosmetics brand whose policy of refusing collaboration with endorsers seen as contradicting its religious values went viral on TikTok in February 2026. This study aims to examine how B Erl Cosmetics' endorsement strategy on TikTok is perceived as authentic by Generation Z consumers and how this perception shapes brand trust and the brand's halal image. The study employs a qualitative case study approach through semi-structured in-depth interviews with five purposively selected Generation Z informants, analyzed using Reflexive Thematic Analysis grounded in Brand Authenticity Theory. The findings show that all informants perceived B Erl Cosmetics' endorser selection policy as a genuine commitment to protecting its halal brand image rather than mere image- building, although the basis of this perceived sincerity varied, ranging from the owner's personal struggle narrative to reputational-risk reasoning and intuitive belief, while most informants also reported increased brand trust and positive purchase intention. The study concludes that the religiously grounded endorsement policy is perceived as authentic by consumers, thereby strengthening brand trust and the halal brand image of B Erl Cosmetics among Generation Z TikTok users.

latest.title: Brand resilience under environmental threat: competing mediating roles of perceived value and environmental concern in seafood purchase intentions
latest.abstract: Purpose This study investigates how brand image shapes seafood purchase intentions under environmental threat. Drawing on the stimulus–organism–response (S–O–R) framework, it examines the competing mediating roles of perceived value and environmental concern. Design/methodology/approach Using a systematic sampling approach, this study collected 319 valid questionnaires from coastal consumers in Guangdong Province, China. Structural equation modeling was used to test the dual-mediation model involving perceived value and environmental concern. Findings Brand image positively influences both perceived value and environmental concern. Perceived value enhances purchase intention, while environmental concern suppresses it. Both variables significantly mediate the brand–purchase relationship in opposing directions, with an overall positive indirect effect, suggesting that brand resilience endures despite ecological concerns. Originality/value This study contributes by modeling competing psychological mediators in seafood consumption under environmental threat, an area that has received limited attention in existing literature. It reveals consumer ambivalence during ecological crises: while strong brands retain appeal, environmental risk awareness weakens purchasing confidence. The findings offer actionable insights for seafood marketers on sustaining brand resilience through value communication and transparent sustainability practices.

latest.title: Integrating Social Influence Theory and the Theory of Planned Behavior to Explain Green Drinkware Purchase Intention among Jakarta’s Emerging Adults: The Moderating Role of Economic Constraints
latest.abstract: This study investigated how digital social influence shaped green drinkware purchase intentions among emerging adults in Jakarta by integrating Social Influence Theory (SIT) and the Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB). A quantitative survey was conducted among 400 Jakarta residents aged 20–29 who were familiar with green drinkware and had previously used or purchased such products. The collected data were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM). The findings revealed that social media engagement positively influenced attitudes and subjective norms, with the relationship between social media engagement and subjective norms exhibiting the strongest path coefficient. Both attitudes and subjective norms positively influenced green label awareness, which, in turn, strengthened green brand trust. Green brand trust subsequently had a positive effect on green purchase intention. Although economic constraints exhibited a negative moderating effect, this relationship was not statistically significant. These findings indicated that social media served not merely as an information dissemination channel but also as a normative environment that shaped consumers' perceptions, attitudes, and behavioral intentions. Furthermore, green purchase intention emerged through a multistage process involving social influence, psychological responses, environmental information awareness, and brand trust. The study contributed to the integration of SIT and TPB by demonstrating the interconnected mechanisms underlying environmentally responsible purchasing intentions. From a practical perspective, the findings highlighted the importance of leveraging social proof in marketing communications, providing credible environmental labeling information, strengthening consume

latest.title: Human Resource Management and Pro-Environmental Behaviour of Young People in the Context of Industry 5.0
latest.abstract: Industry 5.0 shifts the focus of enterprise transformation towards sustainability and human-centricity. This places new demands on human resource management (HRM), which needs to understand the pro-environmental values and behaviour of young people as the future workforce. The aim of the paper is to identify how young people in Slovakia experience climate change, to what extent their pro-environmental attitudes are reflected in their economic decisions and what this implies for HRM. The empirical basis is an online questionnaire survey of 427 young adults aged 18 to 30 in Slovakia in 2026. Climate change experience is measured by the Climate Change Anxiety Scale, and economic decision-making by willingness to pay more for green products and services, saving for green investments and limiting expenditures due to climate change. Descriptive statistics are used. Young people experience climate change mainly through behavioural engagement in everyday sustainable practices, whereas cognitive-emotional and functional impairment are rare. When saving for green investments, economic motives, particularly reducing household costs and gaining energy independence, prevail over environmental ones, and decisions requiring financial resources are made only by a minority. The pro-environmental economic decisions of the future workforce thus follow primarily an economic logic. For HRM, this implies connecting sustainability initiatives with tangible employee benefits, such as support for green investments or sustainable mobility, and bridging individual values and organisational environmental goals through green HRM practices.

latest.title: When Does Sustainable Storytelling Foster Advocacy Intention? The Mediating Roles of Perceived ESG Authenticity and Emotional Brand Resonance, and the Moderating Role of Green Scepticism in Digital Ecosystems
latest.venue: Corporate Social Responsibility and Environmental Management
latest.abstract: ABSTRACT Amid widespread greenwashing and consumer scepticism, brands struggle to convert sustainability commitments into advocacy intention. This study examines sustainable digital storytelling encompassing narrative environmental framing (NEF), interactive sustainability co‐narration (ISC), and temporal impact visualisation (TIV) as a distinct communicative mode. Drawing on narrative transportation, signalling, and attribution theories, we develop a moderated‐mediation model linking these storytelling dimensions to sustainable consumption advocacy intention (SCAI) through perceived ESG authenticity (ESGA) and emotional brand resonance (EBR), with green scepticism (GSCP) as a boundary condition. A three‐wave, time‐lagged survey of 512 Vietnamese consumers confirms that all three storytelling dimensions enhance ESGA and EBR, which in turn predict advocacy intention, with no statistically significant residual direct effects of storytelling on advocacy. However, green scepticism attenuates these effects, diminishing compelling narratives' motivational impact. This study extends narrative transportation theory to the sustainable digital branding domain, identifies a dual cognitive‐affective pathway through which storytelling generates advocacy intention, and establishes green scepticism as a boundary condition that attenuates advocacy conversion even when authenticity and resonance perceptions are strong.

latest.title: Why Does Gamification Fail? The Impact Mechanisms of Gamification Design Flaws on Consumers' Continuous Purchase Intention
latest.abstract: ABSTRACT Although e‐commerce platforms widely implement gamification designs, the potential negative effects on consumers and the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. To address this gap, this study employs a two‐stage mixed‐methods approach to uncover the influence mechanisms of gamification design flaws. In Study 1, we collected 24,749 consumer comments describing negative experiences with gamified shopping festivals. By combining BERTopic modeling with a human‐LLM collaboration, we identified seven latent concepts. Further analysis grounded in psychological reactance theory and affective events theory indicated that four gamification design flaws, namely narrative rhythm disruption, game interaction complexity, reward value distortion, and gameplay replaceability, affect consumers' continuous purchase intention through perceived manipulation and frustration. In Study 2, we collected survey responses from 398 consumers who participated in the gamified shopping festivals and used PLS‐SEM to test the proposed hypotheses. This research deepens understanding of the adverse side of gamification, contributes to theoretical perspectives on the mechanisms of gamification design flaws, and provides novel insights for optimizing gamification in e‐commerce platforms.

latest.title: Religiosity and consumer behaviour among Millennials and Gen Z: does gender make a difference?
latest.abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine how religiosity is associated with consumer behaviour among Millennials and Gen Z in a highly religious emerging market. It proposes the spiritual cognitive consumption theory (SCCT), a dual pathway framework, and provides preliminary empirical support for its overall predictive validity. However, these two pathways were not directly measured; future experimental research is needed to isolate each mechanism. Design/methodology/approach Survey data from 400 Nigerian respondents were analysed using structural equation modelling. Gender significantly moderates this relationship: women tend to show a stronger association between religiosity and relational aspects (e.g. brand trust, emotional congruity), whereas men focus more on instrumental outcomes (e.g. product functionality, religious symbolism). Findings The SCCT framework provides a nuanced understanding of the tension between spiritual devotion and market-based consumption. The findings offer marketers gender-sensitive, faith-conscious strategies and position SCCT as a robust theoretical tool for understanding spirituality, cognition and consumption in evolving digital economies. Social implications The study contributes to sustainable development goal (SDG) 10 (Reduced Inequalities) and SDG 12 (Responsible Consumption and Production) by providing insights into inclusive, faith-sensitive marketing practices in the Global South. Originality/value The originality of this study lies in the development of the SCCT framework, which integrates spirituality, cognition and consumption into a dual pathway model. This offers a novel theoretical lens for understanding consumer behaviour in religious emerging markets.

latest.title: Beyond the Environment: How Green Innovation Drives the Political, Economic and Social Performance of Chemical SMEs through Green Human Resource Practices
latest.abstract: Small and medium-sized firms, particularly those in polluting industries, are facing increasing pressure. They must demonstrate that green innovation is not only good for the environment, but also beneficial for business. Researchers have always viewed human resource management as the driving element behind green innovation. They have also measured innovation primarily by the environmental benefits it produces. Two questions remain unanswered: whether green innovation benefits the firm's political, economic, and social standing in addition to the environment, and whether enterprises that innovate green must also develop green human resource practices for that innovation to work. This study begins with innovation and connects it to green human resource practices, based on the natural resource concept. It investigates how these concepts affect economic and social performance in small chemical enterprises. Data from 600 personnel in Faisalabad, Lahore, and Multan, Pakistan, were analyzed using least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) in SmartPLS 4. The findings demonstrate that green innovation improves political, economic, and social performance while also strengthening green human resource practices. Green human resource practices, in turn, have a favorable impact on all three types of performance and somewhat mitigate the effect of green innovation on each. The model explains 39.8 percent of the variance in performance (34.0 percent in economic performance and 32.7 percent in social performance). The data reveal that green innovation benefits SMEs most when it is combined with recruitment, training, appraisal, awards, and employee engagement. According to the report, green skills provide not only economic but also social and political benefits. It advises ow

latest.title: Human Resource Management for ESG: A Structured Literature Review and Research Agenda
latest.venue: International Journal of Advanced Multidisciplinary Research and Studies
latest.abstract: Purpose: Environmental, social and governance (ESG) commitments are made in boardrooms but carried out by employees. This review asks what the literature knows about how human resource management (HRM) contributes to each ESG pillar, through which mechanisms, under what conditions, and how HRM itself is captured in ESG disclosure. Design/methodology/approach: Guided by the assembling, arranging and assessing stages of the SPAR-4-SLR protocol, we combined keyword searches of Scopus and Web of Science (articles published from 2011 onward) with backward and forward citation chaining and selected a purposive set of 29 core empirical studies, which were coded on HRM stream, ESG pillar, level of analysis, design and context, and 17 prior reviews were used to position the contribution. Findings: The evidence base is lopsided. Over half of the coded studies address the environmental pillar through green HRM, mostly with cross-sectional employee surveys from Asian service and manufacturing firms. The social pillar is studied mainly through socially responsible HRM and employee well-being, while governance appears only in work on ESG-linked executive pay and board diversity. Three streams that rarely cite one another, namely micro-level HRM research, corporate finance studies of employee welfare and accounting research on disclosure, are integrated here into a framework linking HRM architecture, mechanisms, pillar-specific outcomes, disclosure and firm value, with a feedback loop from ESG performance to HR investment. Originality/value: To our knowledge, the review is the first to organise HRM-ESG research by pillar rather than by HR practice and to connect it with the new generation of human capital reporting rules (ESRS S1, ISO 30414:2025, the SEC human capital rule and Vietnam

latest.title: From others to the self: Influence mechanisms of multiple social agents on sustainable consumption
latest.abstract: 摘要： 可持续消费研究长期聚焦个体消费者的心理与行为机制, 无力弥合可持续态度与实际消费行为之间的显著差距。理论演进的脉络梳理表明, 可持续消费的个体选择会受到消费者社会关系网络中多元社会主体的复杂影响。本文系统梳理个体、群体和组织层面的社会主体对消费者可持续消费的影响, 并基于自我决定理论提出了以基本心理需求和动机内化连续体为核心的社会主体影响机制与效应框架。未来研究应重点探讨如何完善多元主体对个体可持续消费的影响机制框架、拓展社会主体的研究边界、推动可持续消费的集体行动研究转向, 从而为破解可持续消费知易行难的现实困境拓展理论空间与实践路径。

latest.title: Lowering the climate impact of academic conferences: lessons learned from two Swedish cases
latest.abstract: Academics, universities and activists increasingly scrutinize academic conferences for their carbon footprints, with questions being raised about the justification for events with very high emissions. This article reports carbon emissions from two international academic conferences held in Sweden, with mean per-participant emissions of 0.17 and 0.19 tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent (t CO2e) (or 0.15 and 0.17 t CO2e, respectively, including virtual participants). Of total calculated emissions, 93% to 95% came from travel (over 80% by air), while accommodation accounted for an estimated 5%. The emissions from digital technology for remote participation were negligible. Emissions were comparatively low in comparison to other international academic conferences. Both events targeted sustainability-related communities and aimed to reduce operational emissions. Our findings suggest three key factors to explain the observed low emissions. First, both conferences had predominantly regional participation, with comparatively few intercontinental attendees (1% and 3%). Second, both conferences were held in locations that are easily accessible by public and land-based transport. Finally, both events offered online participation as an alternative to in-person attendance. This article concludes that conference reach (international vs. regional) has the greatest impact on emissions. For a given geographic extent, organizers should support and promote low-carbon mobility, for example by choosing a conference location with good public, land-based connections and offering meaningful online participation. We also recommend consistently assessing carbon emissions for any academic conference and promoting low-carbon travel for attendees.

latest.title: Greening Consumer Behavior in Bangladesh: Unraveling the Influence of Environmental Attitude and Social Media Marketing on Green Purchase Intentions
latest.venue: Asian Journal of Economics Business and Accounting
latest.abstract: Background: Green purchase intention in Bangladesh may be associated with social media communication, environmental attitudes, product knowledge and consumers' perceived capacity to make sustainable choices. Objective: This study examined the direct associations of social media marketing, environmental attitude, green product knowledge and perceived behavioural control with green purchase intention, together with the mediating role of product knowledge and the moderating role of perceived behavioural control. Methods: An online, self-administered questionnaire yielded 345 responses, of which 300 were retained for analysis. Participants were selected through purposive sampling. Partial least squares structural equation modelling was used to examine the proposed relationships. Results: Social media marketing (β = 0.372, p < 0.001), environmental attitude (β = 0.137, p <0.05), green product knowledge (β = 0.177, p <0.01) and perceived behavioural control (β = 0.124, p <0.05) were positively associated with green purchase intention. Green product knowledge partially mediated the associations of social media marketing (indirect β = 0.045, p <0.05) and environmental attitude (indirect β = 0.032, p <0.05) with purchase intention. Perceived behavioural control also moderated the social media marketing–purchase intention association (β = 0.100, p <0.05). The model explained 28% of the variance in green purchase intention. Conclusion: The findings suggest that informative digital promotion, environmental attitudes, product knowledge and perceived purchasing control are relevant to green purchase intentions among the surveyed Bangladeshi consumers. The cross-sectional design does not establish causality.

latest.title: The Impact of Sustainability Labels on Consumer Purchase Intentions and Buying Behaviour
latest.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
latest.abstract: As the world of business moves at a fast pace towards a greener future, sustainability has transformed from being a mere marketing trend to a vital core strategic policy in the world of business. This paper explores the impact of sustainability labelling on purchase behaviour of the consumer amongst a targeted group of 100 Gen-Z and Young Adult respondents. Using a quantitative research methodology, primary data is collected with a structured digital survey via Google forms and analysed with percentage analysis. The research scope is defined on assessing the response of Gen Z consumer in general retail markets, meeting the 4 major objectives of this research. The impacts of eco labelling influence on purchasing decisions, the role of consumer awareness and trust in purchase decision, the effect of pricing premiums and product quality and the attitude-behaviour gap that does not transition to action at point of purchase. Empirically, our data suggests that though 82.0% of the respondents do show some form of searching for sustainability labels, and 71.0% have some moderate-strong influences towards the labels in making their final purchase, there is still a lot of scepticism and pricing barriers. Where 46.0% suggests that a high price difference, compared to other products, is the main reason for going back to normal alternatives. Ultimately, the findings offer actionable insights for businesses to bridge this gap of intention vs behaviour, genuine brand trust, and push for sustainable growth of the market.

latest.title: Effects of mimicry style, identity positioning, and description style on trust and usage intention in AI pet healthcare platforms
latest.abstract: With the continuous advancement of artificial intelligence applications in the field of pet healthcare, AI pet medical platforms have gradually become important tools for pet health management. However, in contexts characterized by high emotional involvement and high uncertainty, users’ trust in and adoption of such platforms still face significant challenges. Based on trust calibration theory, uncertainty management theory, and the Computers Are Social Actors paradigm, this study adopts a 2 × 2 × 2 between-subjects experimental design to examine the effects of mimicry style (anthropomorphic design versus zoomorphic design), identity positioning (expert-authoritative versus friendly-companion), and description style (lay terminology versus professional terminology) on users’ cognitive trust, affective attachment, and usage intention. A total of 400 valid samples were collected, and the hypotheses were tested using analysis of variance and mediation analysis. The results indicate that zoomorphic design significantly enhances affective attachment and usage intention and exerts a partial mediating effect on usage intention through affective attachment and cognitive trust. Expert-authoritative identity positioning significantly increases cognitive trust and usage intention, whereas the mediating role of affective attachment is not significant. Descriptive style shows no significant direct effect on usage intention, but professional terminology exerts a mediating effect on usage intention through cognitive trust. In addition, a significant interaction effect is found between mimicry style and identity positioning. The findings suggest that user adoption of AI pet medical platforms is jointly driven by both affective and cognitive pathways, with cognitive trust playing a more

latest.title: Green nudges for sustainable e-commerce: a bibliometric analysis
latest.abstract: In view of the rising online consumption and growing environmental concerns, e-commerce platforms face a critical dilemma. They need to influence consumer choices toward sustainability without compromising user autonomy or crossing ethical boundaries. Incorporating green nudges—subtle design prompts intended to steer users toward more eco-friendly decisions—has emerged as a promising yet controversial strategy. This study conducts a systematic literature review, following PRISMA guidelines, to examine how green nudges are used in digital commerce and how effective they are in promoting sustainable purchasing patterns. A comprehensive Scopus search of studies on green nudging in e-commerce reveals a 28.21% annual publication growth rate and an average of 25.68 citations across 33 countries. Bibliometric and content analysis reveals emerging themes and identifies the contextual factors that shape the success of these interventions. The findings highlight the potential of green nudges but also reveal key challenges, including inconsistent implementation, culturally variable outcomes, and ethical concerns about manipulation. The review underscores the need for a more nuanced, context-sensitive approach to green nudge design, accounting for user demographics, digital architecture, and behavioral science. This work both synthesizes current knowledge and proposes a research agenda to guide ethical and effective use of green nudges in sustainable e-commerce.

latest.title: Collaborative Sourcing Strategy and Performance of Alcoholic Beverages Manufacturing Companies in Kenya
latest.venue: International Journal of Supply Chain and Logistics
latest.abstract: Purpose: The main objective of the study was to examine the relationship between collaborative sourcing strategy and performance of alcoholic beverage manufacturing companies in Kenya. Methodology: The study adopted a positivist research philosophy and explanatory research design. The unit of analysis was 30 alcoholic beverage manufacturing companies in Kenya, while the unit of observation comprised heads of finance, administration, procurement, ICT, operations, marketing and logistics departments. The target population was 210 heads of departments. The study adopted stratified random sampling. Both primary and secondary data were used. Secondary data were obtained from annual company reports, while primary data were collected using semi-structured questionnaires.
